ai_comments.171: Mandates the Secretary‑General to notify Members at least 60 days in advance of the opening of a regular session. DGACM/Conference Management implements this Secretariat notification and session‑planning function (see PPB responsibilities for facilitating Assembly sessions and planning/coordination of conference services).
ai_comments.185: Requires the Secretary‑General to inform other Members immediately when a Member requests convening a special session. DGACM operationally supports such communications and the logistics of convening sessions as part of Secretariat conference‑servicing responsibilities.
ai_comments.189: Obliges the Secretary‑General to notify Members of special sessions (timing specified). This is an operational Secretariat duty carried out through conference‑management processes that DGACM provides (meeting scheduling/notifications in the PPB).
ai_comments.193: Directs that copies of the notice convening each session be addressed to other principal organs and specialized agencies. DGACM (Secretariat conference services) handles distribution of session notices and related outreach across UN organs as reflected in its conference‑management remit.
ai_comments.198: States that the provisional agenda for a regular session shall be drawn up by the Secretary‑General and communicated to Members at least sixty days before opening. DGACM provides the secretariat processes and publishing/distribution support for agendas and related documentation in its programme of work (agenda management and e‑services noted in the PPB).
ai_comments.211: Requires that supplementary items be placed on a supplementary list which shall be communicated to Members at least twenty days before opening. The communication and maintenance of agenda/supplementary lists are Secretariat tasks implemented through DGACM’s documentation and meeting‑planning functions.
ai_comments.306: Provides that the Secretary‑General shall act in that capacity at all meetings and may designate a member of the Secretariat to act in his place. This assigns meeting representation and delegation authority to Secretariat staff — functions that DGACM carries out in providing procedural and technical secretariat support to the Assembly and committees (PPB subprogramme responsibilities).
ai_comments.308: States that the Secretary‑General shall provide and direct the staff required by the General Assembly and any committees or subsidiary organs. DGACM is the Secretariat entity charged with provisioning and directing the conference‑servicing and documentation staff (explicitly reflected in the PPB programme responsibilities for staffing, temporary assistance and global capacity planning).
ai_comments.311: Explicit Secretariat duty: 'The Secretariat shall receive, translate, print and distribute documents, reports and resolutions ... interpret speeches ... prepare, print and circulate the records of the session ... distribute all documents ... and, generally, perform all other work which the Assembly may require.' This directly mandates the core activities that DGACM’s subprogrammes (documentation, meetings, publishing, interpretation, verbatim reporting and distribution) are established to implement in the PPB.
ai_comments.327: Provides that speeches in any of the six languages shall be interpreted into the other five languages. This creates an obligation for interpretation services that the Secretariat must provide — a direct operational mandate implemented by DGACM’s meetings/interpretation services (subprogramme 4 and related duty‑station activities in the PPB).
ai_comments.332: Requires that verbatim or summary records shall be drawn up as soon as possible in the languages of the General Assembly. The preparation and issuance of verbatim/summary records are Secretariat functions implemented by DGACM (verbatim reporting, records processing and publishing services reflected in the PPB).
ai_comments.335: Specifies that during sessions the Journal of the United Nations shall be published in the languages of the Assembly. Publication of the Journal is a Secretariat publishing responsibility — reflected in DGACM’s PPB activities (development and operation of the Journal and eJournal platforms).
ai_comments.337: States that all resolutions and other documents shall be published in the languages of the General Assembly. This imposes multilingual publishing and simultaneous‑issuance obligations that DGACM’s documentation and publishing subprogrammes are mandated and resourced to carry out in the PPB.
ai_comments.345: Rule 58(a): Verbatim records of the meetings of the General Assembly and the First Committee 'shall be drawn up by the Secretariat and submitted to those organs after approval by the presiding officer.' This is an explicit Secretariat mandate implemented operationally by DGACM’s verbatim reporting and records subprogramme.
ai_comments.346: Rule 58(b): Sound recordings of meetings 'shall be made by the Secretariat.' Provision and custody of sound recordings are Secretariat responsibilities that DGACM executes (recording/transcription and archival functions described in the PPB).
ai_comments.349: Requires that resolutions adopted by the General Assembly shall be communicated by the Secretary‑General to Members within fifteen days after the close of the session. The timely communication and distribution of adopted resolutions is an operational Secretariat task performed via DGACM’s documentation and publishing channels.

ai_comments.58: Directs the Secretary‑General to communicate, as soon as possible, the names (and any curricula vitae) of candidates submitted by Governments to Member States. This creates a Secretariat task to process and disseminate nominations; DGACM’s PPB identifies the Department as responsible for procedural and technical secretariat support to the General Assembly and for communication/administrative handling of intergovernmental business (see overall orientation and subprogramme responsibilities for secretariat support), so DGACM would implement this communicative/administrative function.
ai_comments.60: Requires the Secretary‑General to prepare the alphabetical list of duly nominated candidates and submit it to the General Assembly for election. Preparing and submitting electoral documentation and lists is an administrative/secretariat service; DGACM’s mandate and PPB (provision of procedural and technical secretariat support to the General Assembly and related bodies) indicate that the Department carries out such Secretariat tasks.
ai_comments.98: Directs the Secretary‑General to make available, so far as he is able, the staff and facilities required by the Commission to fulfil its task. This is an instruction to the Secretariat to provide staffing and facilities support; DGACM’s PPB explicitly assigns the Department responsibility for substantive and technical secretariat support, conference‑servicing facilities and related staffing arrangements, so DGACM would be responsible for implementing this provision.
ai_comments.109: States that the Secretary‑General will provide, when necessary and within budget limits, for the expenses of consultations of experts (in connection with Commission work). This obliges the Secretariat to arrange and fund expert consultations and associated administrative arrangements; DGACM’s PPB shows the Department coordinates consultations, manages meeting support and administers related resources (programme support and conference services), indicating DGACM would implement these logistical and funding arrangements.
ai_comments.181: Provides that when the Commission considers a draft satisfactory it shall request the Secretary‑General to issue it as a Commission document and that the Secretariat shall give all necessary publicity to the document, with explanations and supporting material. This is a direct instruction to the Secretariat to publish, publicize and distribute Commission documents. DGACM’s PPB assigns documentation, publishing and distribution functions (subprogramme 3 and subprogramme 4) — simultaneous issuance, publication and dissemination — so DGACM would carry out these publication/distribution obligations.
ai_comments.227: Directs the Secretary‑General, after consultation with the Commission, to draw up a list of national and international organizations concerned with questions of international law for the purpose of distribution of Commission documents, and to endeavour to include at least one national organization of each Member. This tasks the Secretariat with preparing distribution networks/lists and distributing documents; DGACM’s PPB includes publishing, distribution and outreach functions (maintaining portals, distributing parliamentary documentation and outreach to organizations), linking this paragraph to DGACM implementation responsibility.
ai_comments.234: Instructs the Secretary‑General to do the necessary preparatory work for the commencement of the Commission’s activity (preparatory Secretariat work, e.g., on items referred by the General Assembly such as the draft declaration on rights and duties of States). This is an instruction to the Secretariat to undertake preparatory administrative and substantive support; DGACM’s PPB identifies the Department as the provider of procedural and substantive secretariat support for the Assembly and its subsidiary bodies, so DGACM would be expected to implement this preparatory work.

ai_comments.36: Text: “The Secretary-General shall make available to the Commission the appropriate staff and facilities required by the Commission to fulfil its task.” This directs the Secretary‑General to provide staff and facilities to support the Commission. DGACM (per its PPB) is the UN entity responsible for providing procedural and technical secretariat support, conference services and the staffing/facilities necessary for intergovernmental bodies (see PPB: responsibility for procedural and technical secretariat support and conference‑servicing across duty stations, e.g. 2.1(a),(c); programme support description). Thus paragraph 36 creates an obligation that the Secretariat implement — operationally delivered by DGACM — by supplying staff, facilities and conference‑servicing.
ai_comments.56: Text: “Requests the Secretary‑General, pending the election of the Commission, to carry out the preparatory work necessary for the organization of the work of the Commission and, in particular:” This instructs the Secretary‑General to undertake preparatory organizational work (invitations, collection of submissions, coordination) prior to the Commission’s election. Those Secretariat preparatory and organizational tasks are precisely the kinds of procedural/secretariat functions DGACM performs (PPB: DGACM provides substantive and technical secretariat support, planning and coordination of conference services, and document/service management for intergovernmental bodies — see PPB summary and subprogramme strategies such as 2.1(a),(c), 2.33(d)).
ai_comments.57: Text (subparagraph to 56 (a)): “To invite Member States to submit in writing before 1 July 1967 ... comments on a programme of work to be undertaken by the Commission...” This is a specific instruction to the Secretary‑General to issue invitations and collect Member State submissions. DGACM’s PPB shows it implements such tasks (member‑state communications, circulation and management of submissions and agenda items, see PPB: provision of procedural secretariat support and management of documentation and meeting requests — e.g. 2.1(a); 2.33(d)).
ai_comments.58: Text (subparagraph to 56 (b)): “To request similar comments from the organs and organizations referred to in paragraph 8 (f) and (g) and in paragraph 12 of section II above.” This directs the Secretary‑General to solicit inputs from other UN organs and organizations. DGACM routinely carries out inter‑org coordination and solicitation/management of submissions as part of its secretariat and documentation services (see PPB: coordination with other organs and providing substantive and technical secretariat support, e.g. 2.1(c),(f) and 2.33(d)), so this paragraph imposes actionable tasks implemented by DGACM.

ai_comments.25: Operative paragraph 6 (“Requests the Chairman of the Committee on Conferences and the Secretary‑General to maintain their contacts … in order to assist those organs in making better use of their services”). This directs the Secretary‑General and the Committee on Conferences to engage with United Nations organs that have under‑utilized conference‑servicing resources so as to assist them to use those services better. The Department for General Assembly and Conference Management (DGACM) provides the Secretariat support to the Committee on Conferences and is the Organization’s conference‑servicing arm (see PPB paras. 2.1(c), 2.2 and subprogrammes on planning/coordination of conference services). DGACM would therefore be the operational entity to prepare and deliver the assistance, outreach and technical support called for by this paragraph (e.g., through planning, consultations, and service adjustments).
ai_comments.139: Operative paragraph 4 under “Control and Limitation of Documentation” (“Requests the Secretary‑General to establish a standard format for final reports of special conferences … and to provide guidelines for the preparation and editing of those reports”). This is an explicit request to the Secretary‑General to set documentation standards and guidance. DGACM’s PPB identifies its core responsibility for documentation, publishing and editorial standards (see PPB paras. 2.1(a),(c); subprogramme 3 and subprogramme 4 descriptions such as paras. 2.46 and 2.59). DGACM would therefore be the principal Secretariat service responsible for developing and implementing the standard format and editorial guidelines referenced in this paragraph.
ai_comments.155: Operative paragraph beginning “Requests the Secretary‑General to submit information to the Committee on Conferences at its organizational session … to assist the Committee in establishing its work programme on a biennial basis …” This directs the Secretary‑General to provide information to the Committee on Conferences to assist its planning. DGACM provides substantive and technical secretariat support to the Committee on Conferences and to the organization and calendar of meetings (see PPB paras. 2.1(c), 2.20 and the Committee on Conferences terms noted in the PPB). DGACM would therefore be responsible for preparing and supplying the information the Secretary‑General is requested to submit.
ai_comments.168: Operative paragraph (“Requests the Secretary‑General to continue his valuable efforts to implement resolution 42/207 C” and to report thereon). Resolution 42/207 C and its follow‑up concern control/limitation of documentation and related Secretariat practices. DGACM’s mandate covers documentation management, publication policies and monitoring implementation of Assembly decisions on conference servicing and documentation (see PPB paras. 2.1, 2.14 and subprogramme 3 activities). While the paragraph addresses the Secretary‑General, DGACM would be the primary Secretariat unit responsible for carrying out the implementation measures and for supplying the reporting requested of the Secretary‑General.

ai_comments.22: Creates a clear obligation that the first session of the Conference of the Parties be held on specific dates. DGACM’s PPB (mandates at paras. 2.1(a) and 2.1(c) and the subprogramme descriptions) shows the Department is responsible for facilitation and provision of procedural and technical secretariat and conference‑servicing support for United Nations conferences and special meetings. Thus paragraph 22 translates into tasks for DGACM to plan, schedule and provide the secretariat, meeting‑servicing, documentation, interpretation and related logistical support required to convene that session.
ai_comments.23: Expresses the Assembly’s acceptance of the Government of Germany’s offer to host the first session in Berlin. While not naming the Department, this decision entails practical arrangements (host‑country liaison, protocol, onsite conference services) that DGACM’s PPB shows it implements (see para. 2.1(c) on conference‑servicing at locations outside Headquarters and para. 2.1(d) on protocol and host‑country liaison). Accordingly, this paragraph gives rise to implementation tasks for DGACM to coordinate logistics and protocol with the host.
ai_comments.24: Decides to include the session in the calendar of conferences and meetings for 1994–1995. DGACM’s mandate (e.g., para. 2.1 and the planning/coordination subprogramme descriptions) includes management of the calendar of conferences/meetings and related scheduling functions. This paragraph therefore directs an administrative action (calendar inclusion and associated scheduling coordination) that DGACM is responsible for implementing.

ai_comments.23: Operative para 1 requests the Secretary‑General to ensure strict implementation of resolutions establishing language arrangements. DGACM (the Department for General Assembly and Conference Management) is the Secretariat entity charged in its PPB with establishing and applying language arrangements, providing authoritative procedural/technical secretariat support and multilingual meeting and documentation services (see PPB paras 2.1(c),(d), 2.2–2.3). Thus this paragraph directs an action (implementation of language arrangements) that DGACM is responsible for carrying out on behalf of the Secretariat.
ai_comments.25: Operative para 3 requests the Secretary‑General to ensure staff appointments follow Article 101 and that recruits have command of at least one working language (and to encourage use of other official languages in promotions). DGACM’s PPB identifies the Department’s role in Secretariat‑wide coordination of multilingualism and in recruitment, training and replenishing language capacity (see PPB paras 2.3, 2.46(f),(g) and related sections on staffing and training). The paragraph thus creates an obligation for the Secretariat that DGACM is mandated to implement or support operationally.
ai_comments.26: Operative para 4 requests the Secretary‑General to ensure, in recruitment and promotion of Secretariat staff, equality of the working languages. DGACM is presented in the PPB as the system‑wide lead on multilingualism and is responsible for policies/standards and coordination (PPB paras 2.2–2.3), so this instruction to the Secretary‑General falls to DGACM to help implement in practice.
ai_comments.31: Operative para 9 urges delegations and the Secretariat to endeavour to avoid holding informal meetings without interpretation. This directly addresses the Secretariat’s conduct of meetings. DGACM’s PPB (subprogramme on meetings and interpretation: paras 2.59–2.60 and results/activities across subprogrammes 2 and 4) shows the Department is responsible for providing interpretation and meeting support, so the paragraph imposes an operational requirement DGACM would need to apply/advice on.
ai_comments.32: Operative para 10 requests the Secretary‑General to report to the General Assembly at its fifty‑second session on implementation of the resolution, particularly on use of official and working languages. DGACM’s PPB identifies the Department as Secretariat‑wide coordinator and system‑wide lead on multilingualism (PPB para 2.3) and describes its role in monitoring, evaluation and reporting on multilingual conference services. Preparing or contributing substantive material for such a report is therefore an implementation task falling to DGACM.

ai_comments.17: Text requests the Secretary‑General, as depositary, to report to the General Assembly at its fifty‑second session on the status of signature and ratifications. DGACM’s mandate to provide substantive/technical secretariat support and to prepare and issue parliamentary documentation (PPB paras. 2.1(a),(c); subprogramme 3 documentation services, para. 2.46) means it would play a central role in producing, translating, issuing and distributing the Secretary‑General’s report to the Assembly.

ai_comments.16: Directs the Secretary-General to prepare a comprehensive report on the High‑level Political Signing Conference in Palermo. The Department for General Assembly and Conference Management (DGACM) provides conference servicing, documentation and publishing support for high‑level meetings (see PPB: provision of secretariat, documentation and publishing services), so DGACM would be the operational unit likely tasked by the Secretary‑General to produce or support preparation, processing and issuance of that report.
ai_comments.364: States that the Secretary‑General shall convene the Conference of the Parties not later than one year after entry into force. DGACM’s mandate includes planning, managing and servicing intergovernmental conferences and meetings (PPB: provision of procedural and technical secretariat support and conference‑servicing across duty stations), so DGACM would be responsible for implementing the convening logistics and related secretariat functions.
ai_comments.375: Provides that the Secretary‑General shall provide the necessary secretariat services to the Conference of the Parties. This is a direct instruction to ensure secretariat support; DGACM’s PPB explicitly assigns it responsibility for substantive and technical secretariat support and high‑quality conference‑servicing (see PPB 2.1(a),(c) and the subprogrammes on planning/coordination, documentation and meetings/publishing), meaning DGACM would implement this obligation.
ai_comments.377: (Article 33(a)) Requires the secretariat to assist the Conference of the Parties in carrying out the activities in article 32 and to make arrangements and provide necessary services for sessions. This maps to DGACM’s operational responsibilities for arranging meetings and providing conference services (PPB: planning/coordination of conference services, meetings and publishing services, and provision of substantive/technical secretariat support), indicating DGACM would carry out these tasks.
ai_comments.378: (Article 33(b)) Requires the secretariat, upon request, to assist States Parties in providing information to the Conference of the Parties. DGACM’s PPB includes documentation, publishing and substantive secretariat support (subprogramme 3 and subprogramme 1 activities on procedural/advisory support and documentation services), so DGACM would be the unit to assist with collecting, preparing and managing such information for States and the Conference.
ai_comments.379: (Article 33(c)) Obligates the secretariat to ensure necessary coordination with the secretariats of relevant international and regional organizations. DGACM’s PPB describes inter‑agency coordination and that the Department will chair and coordinate meetings on language arrangements, documentation and publications (PPB 2.10 and related), so DGACM would implement the required coordination role.

ai_comments.9: Paragraph 9 adopts the Protocol and opens it for signature at United Nations Headquarters in New York. While it does not name a Department, this creates an organizational obligation to host and service signature arrangements at UN Headquarters (signature ceremonies, meeting rooms, participant registration, distribution of documents and related protocol support). The Department for General Assembly and Conference Management’s PPB (see paras. 2.1 (a), 2.1 (c) and 2.202) shows it is responsible for conference-servicing, meeting and documentation support and protocol services at Headquarters, so DGACM would be the implementing service for those tasks.
ai_comments.133: Paragraph 133 provides the specific instruction that the Protocol "shall be open to all States for signature at United Nations Headquarters in New York…". That operational requirement obliges the Organization to receive signatures at Headquarters and to provide the logistical, conference‑servicing and protocol arrangements to enable signature and access by delegations. Those operational duties fall squarely within DGACM’s remit per its PPB (conference‑servicing and protocol functions at Headquarters as described in paras. 2.1 (a), 2.1 (c) and 2.202), so DGACM would be the primary implementing entity.

agenda_item_title: Pattern of conferences.

recurrence_actions.group_title: Pattern of conferences.

ai_comments.14: Requests the Secretary-General, when planning the calendar of conferences and meetings, to avoid simultaneous peak periods and avoid scheduling related bodies too closely together. DGACM (the Department) is responsible for planning and coordinating conference services and the calendar across duty stations (see PPB: overall orientation and subprogramme planning/coordination paragraphs such as 2.33 and the Department’s remit in 2.1). This SG instruction will be implemented operationally by the Department (calendar and meeting planning).
ai_comments.15: Also requests the Secretary-General to ensure that any modification to the calendar of conferences and meetings is implemented strictly in accordance with the mandate of the Committee on Conferences and other relevant GA resolutions. The Department executes conference scheduling and implements Committee on Conferences guidance (PPB 2.1, subprogramme planning/coordination roles such as 2.33), so this directs work the Department will carry out.
ai_comments.31: Requests the Secretary-General to report to the General Assembly through the Committee on Conferences on the methodology that accurately reflects the provision of conference services to regional and other major groupings. DGACM prepares and provides such conference-servicing data and methodologies (PPB: subprogramme 2 planning and coordination; reporting of key performance indicators in 2.37–2.38), so this creates a task that the Department is expected to implement or supply input for.
ai_comments.35: Requests the Secretary-General, when preparing budget proposals for conference services, to ensure that the level of resources proposed for temporary assistance is commensurate with full demand for services. DGACM is responsible for planning and proposing conference-servicing resource needs and for matching temporary assistance to workload (PPB: paragraphs on managing surges, temporary assistance and resource planning, e.g. 2.7, 2.33), so this budgetary instruction falls to the Department to implement.
ai_comments.36: Requests the Secretary-General to continue to report in writing on the utilization rates of interpretation services and conference facilities at all duty stations. DGACM produces utilization statistics and reporting for interpretation and conference facilities across duty stations (PPB: planning/coordination and reporting functions in subprogramme 2 and programme support, e.g. 2.33, 2.37), so this directs reporting tasks implemented by the Department.
ai_comments.37: Also requests the Secretary-General to develop methods and indicators for assessing the performance of conference services (cost-effectiveness, efficiency, productivity) and to report thereon. DGACM is mandated in the PPB to develop harmonized KPIs and provide performance data (see 2.33, 2.37 and programme support on evaluation and data analytics 2.226–2.229), so this instruction creates a requirement the Department will operationalize.
ai_comments.47: Stresses that the Department is responsible for the implementation of policy, formulation of standards and guidelines, overseeing and coordinating United Nations conference services and the overall management of resources under the relevant budget section, while the Offices at Geneva, Vienna and Nairobi remain responsible for day-to-day operational activities. This paragraph explicitly assigns responsibilities to DGACM and is a direct mandate defining the Department’s core functions (matches PPB summary of mandates in 2.1 and the Department’s role throughout the programme).
ai_comments.56: Reiterates the request to the Secretary-General to ensure that documentation is available in accordance with the six‑week rule for distribution simultaneously in the six official languages. DGACM’s subprogramme 3 (Documentation services) is responsible for producing and issuing parliamentary documentation simultaneously in all official languages (PPB: objectives and planned results in 2.45–2.53), so this is an instruction that DGACM will be required to implement.
ai_comments.57: Reiterates deep regret concerning failure of author departments to abide by a prior provision and requests the Secretary-General to take corrective measures to ensure full implementation. Ensuring timely submission and processing of documentation falls to DGACM operationally (see PPB: documentation timeliness and quality mandates in 2.45–2.56); thus SG-directed corrective measures will be executed by the Department.
ai_comments.58: Requests the Secretary-General to take all necessary measures to ensure the compliance of the Secretariat, organizations, bodies and organs with the request contained in paragraph 3 of the section, and to submit a report on violations. Compliance and reporting on documentation and multilingual issuance are functions DGACM carries out (PPB: documentation services and Secretariat-wide multilingual coordination noted in 2.1 and 2.3), so the Department will implement these measures and reporting.
ai_comments.69: Notes that the Department will assign timing of submission of manuscripts taking into account the programme of work of the session and time needed to produce the document simultaneously in six official languages at high quality. This sentence explicitly directs an operational role to DGACM in scheduling and timing for manuscript submission and multilingual processing (directly aligns with PPB subprogramme 3 responsibilities and the Department’s mandate described in 2.1 and 2.46–2.56).
ai_comments.74: Notes with concern the delay in issuance of verbatim and summary records and requests the Secretary-General to take appropriate measures to ameliorate the situation. Processing and issuance of verbatim and summary records are core functions of DGACM (PPB subprogramme 4 Meetings and publishing services and subprogramme 3 documentation/verbati mref; see 2.59–2.66 and 2.48–2.56), so SG measures to reduce delays will be implemented by the Department.
ai_comments.76: Also reiterates the request to the Secretary-General to ensure the communication of resolutions adopted by the General Assembly to Member States within fifteen days of the close of each session. DGACM is responsible for publication and distribution of official documents and records (PPB: publishing and documentation services in subprogrammes 3 and 4, and overall mandate in 2.1), so this is a concrete delivery obligation the Department executes.
ai_comments.96: Requests the Secretary-General to ensure that efforts continue to be made to improve the quality control of language services at all duty stations. DGACM leads and manages language and documentation services and quality assurance (PPB: translation quality management, training and standards in 2.46–2.53), so SG action here will be carried out through the Department.
ai_comments.98: Also reiterates the request to the Secretary-General to ensure continuous dialogue between translation staff and interpretation staff among UN HQ and duty stations and between translation divisions and Member States with regard to standardization of terminology. DGACM is the Secretariat-wide coordinator for multilingualism and maintains terminology resources (PPB: role on multilingualism 2.1, Office of the Coordinator for Multilingualism 2.3, and UNTERM reference in 2.46), so this directs coordination work that the Department implements.
ai_comments.100: Requests the Secretary-General to conduct consultations, with the Member States concerned, on the improvement of the translation services. The Department is responsible for translation/documentation service delivery and for engaging Member States on terminology/quality (PPB: documentation services and outreach in 2.46, 2.54 and UNTERM management), so SG-led consultations will be implemented operationally by DGACM.

ai_comments.485: Directs the Secretary‑General to convene the Conference of the States Parties not later than one year after entry into force. This creates an obligation on the Secretariat to organize and convene the Conference — functions that DGACM’s programme budget explicitly covers (provision of procedural and technical secretariat support, conference planning and meeting services across duty stations; see overview and subprogramme descriptions, e.g., para. 2.1 (facilitation through provision of procedural and technical secretariat support) and subprogramme planning/coordination paragraphs such as 2.33). DGACM would be a primary implementing service for the practical arrangements and servicing needed to convene the Conference.
ai_comments.499: Directs the Secretary‑General to provide the necessary secretariat services to the Conference of the States Parties. That is an explicit Secretariat mandate to deliver secretariat services for the Conference — tasks that fall within DGACM’s remit (DGACM provides substantive and technical secretariat support and conference services for United Nations conferences and intergovernmental bodies; see para. 2.1 and the subprogramme descriptions for documentation, meetings and conference management).
ai_comments.501: Specifies that the secretariat shall assist the Conference of the States Parties in carrying out the activities set forth in article 63 and make arrangements and provide the necessary services for the sessions of the Conference. This operationalizes the secretariat obligation into concrete servicing and arrangements for sessions — activities (meeting planning, conference‑servicing, documentation and logistical support) that DGACM’s PPB explicitly states it delivers (see para. 2.1(c), subprogramme strategies for planning and coordination of conference services (e.g., para. 2.33) and meetings/publishing services).
ai_comments.502: States that, upon request, the secretariat shall assist States Parties in providing information to the Conference as envisaged in article 63. This creates a specific secretariat support role for information handling and assistance to Member States — matching DGACM’s documentation, publishing and information‑services functions (subprogramme 3 and subprogramme 4 activities, and references to providing substantive/technical secretariat support and consolidated e‑services in paras. 2.1, 2.21, 2.46).
ai_comments.503: Requires the secretariat to ensure the necessary coordination with the secretariats of relevant international and regional organizations. DGACM’s PPB notes its inter‑agency coordination and liaison role (e.g., para. 2.10 on chairing/participating in inter‑agency meetings and coordination on multilingualism and conference services) and its responsibility for coordinating conference servicing with other entities, so this paragraph assigns a coordination task that DGACM would be expected to implement as part of Secretariat support.

ai_comments.24: Paragraph 24 requests the Secretary‑General to make provisions for the sessions of the Conference of the Parties and its subsidiary bodies in the proposed programme budget for the 2012–2013 biennium. That is an instruction to the Secretariat to include and resource those meetings in its budget submissions — a task that, in practice, DGACM implements through its conference‑management functions (planning and coordination of conference services, inclusion of meetings in the United Nations calendar, preparation of cost estimates and inputs to the programme budget). The Department’s PPB explicitly describes these responsibilities (e.g., provision of conference‑servicing and budgeting/coordination functions under subprogrammes 2 and programme support and the Department’s role in the UN calendar and budgetary provisions), so this paragraph creates an obligation that DGACM would be expected to operationalize.

ai_comments.26: Paragraph 26 directs the Secretary‑General “to enable adequate institutional focus on the needs of small island developing States and provide effective support for the third International Conference on Small Island Developing States.” This is a directive to the Secretary‑General to provide conference-related support. The Department for General Assembly and Conference Management (DGACM) is the Secretariat entity responsible for conference services and substantive/technical secretariat support (see PPB: overall mandates in paras. 2.1(a), 2.1(c) and 2.1(d); planning and coordination of conference services, paras. 2.33, 2.72, 2.112, 2.152; and meetings/publishing services, paras. 2.59, 2.99, 2.139 and 2.178). Therefore DGACM would be expected to implement the Secretary‑General’s obligation in this paragraph by providing the planning, coordination, meeting servicing, documentation, interpretation, publishing and protocol support for that Conference.

title: Strengthening And Enhancing The Effective Functioning Of The Human Rights Treaty Body System
subtitle: Resolution
note: Issued in GAOR, 68th sess., Suppl. no. 49.
author: UN. General Assembly (68th sess. : 2013-2014)
agenda_item_title: United Nations reform: measures and proposals.

ai_comments.31: Decides that annual reports of treaty bodies are not to contain separately published documents — this is a General Assembly decision affecting how treaty-body documentation is prepared and published. DGACM’s PPB shows it is responsible for parliamentary/documentation services (subprogramme 3; see 2.45–2.53, 2.46 strategy and 2.57 deliverables) and would be expected to implement changes to documentation production and publication formats arising from this decision.
ai_comments.42: Decides to establish a 10,700-word limit for each document produced by human rights treaty bodies (and recommends word limits for stakeholders). This creates a requirement that affects document processing and editorial control. DGACM’s documentation service (subprogramme 3: translation/editing/desktop publishing; see 2.46(a),(d), 2.50–2.56) implements and enforces such limits in the production workflow.
ai_comments.43: Decides to establish specific word limits for State party documentation (initial and subsequent reports, common core documents) and calls on treaty bodies to limit questions — this imposes constraints on the volume and format of documentation to be processed. DGACM’s documentation and publishing subprogrammes (subprogramme 3 and subprogramme 4; see 2.46, 2.59 and the discussion of timeliness/simultaneous issuance 2.48–2.56, 2.61–2.69) are the Secretariat units that would operationalize these limits in document intake, editing and issuance.
ai_comments.58: Decides to issue summary records in one working language and not to translate the pending backlog of summary records, while aiming to provide verbatim records in all official languages by alternative methods. This is a decision on the form and language of records and on issuance priorities. DGACM directly provides verbatim reporting, summary records, and publishing services (subprogramme 4 meetings and publishing services and subprogramme 3 documentation; see 2.59(a), 2.48–2.56, 2.61–2.69) and would be responsible for implementing these changes to record production and dissemination.
ai_comments.59: Decides that, at the request of any State party, a summary record of its meeting with a treaty body shall be translated into the UN official language used by that State party — this creates an operational requirement for translation and issuance on request. DGACM’s documentation services (subprogramme 3: translation/editing/précis-writing; see 2.46(a),(d) and 2.48–2.56) are the Secretariat function that would perform those translations and manage fulfilment of such requests.
ai_comments.60: Decides on the identification/allocation of meeting time to treaty bodies and explicitly requests the Secretary‑General to provide the corresponding financial and human resources. DGACM is the Secretariat entity responsible for planning and managing meetings and conference-servicing resources across duty stations (see 2.1(a),(c), 2.2, subprogramme 2 planning and coordination, and programme support 2.226–2.231) and would implement the allocation of meeting time and associated servicing resources.
ai_comments.61: Specifies the method for allocating weeks for review of State party reports (assumed review rates) as part of the meeting-time allocation (26(a)). This operational specification requires scheduling and provision of conference services. DGACM’s work on planning of intergovernmental meetings and tools (subprogramme 2: planning and coordination; see 2.33(a),(e), and references to e-deleGATE and scheduling in 2.20–2.30) is directly implicated in implementing this allocation.
ai_comments.62: Specifies additional allocation of meeting time for committees dealing with individual communications (method and time per communication). This places concrete scheduling and servicing requirements on the Secretariat. DGACM’s conference-servicing and meetings subprogrammes (subprogramme 4 meetings and publishing services and subprogramme 2 planning and coordination; see 2.59, 2.33 and performance measures for meetings and interpretation 2.63–2.66) would operationalize these allocations.
ai_comments.63: Establishes an additional margin (5% target increase, temporary 15% for 2015–2017) to prevent backlogs in meeting-time allocation — an explicit planning/resourcing target that the Secretariat must address. DGACM is responsible for surge planning, workforce/capacity management and temporary assistance to handle demand (see 2.7, 2.59(b), and programme support on capacity/planning 2.226–2.229), so it would implement measures to meet this target.
ai_comments.64: Calls for adequate allocation of financial and human resources to treaty bodies whose main mandated role is to carry out field visits. This is a resource direction to the Secretary‑General with operational implications for meeting/field support. DGACM’s mandate covers conference services, planning and coordination (including servicing of meetings and related logistics) across duty stations (see 2.1(a),(c), subprogramme 2 and programme support sections), and DGACM would be the implementing service for the Secretariat’s provision of meeting and documentation support related to such field activities, as applicable.
ai_comments.65: Decides that meeting-time allocations will be reviewed biennially on the basis of reporting over the previous four years and amended at the request of the Secretary‑General in line with budgetary procedures; also decides not to reduce prior permanent allocations. This establishes a process/timetable that the Secretariat must follow in scheduling and budgeting. DGACM is the Secretariat conference-management programme that prepares schedules, harmonized indicators and inputs for budget/resource allocation (see 2.33, 2.37–2.38 on reporting of KPIs and global harmonization, and programme support responsibilities 2.226–2.231) and would implement the review and any resulting scheduling/budget changes.
ai_comments.66: Requests the Secretary‑General to take into account the meeting time needed (per paragraphs 26 and 27) in his future biennial programme budget for the human rights treaty body system, including specific requirements for field visits. This is a direct instruction to budget for meeting-time needs. DGACM is the programme that is budgeted for and that provides the conference services and staffing that correspond to those budget lines (see resource and programme sections 2.190–2.197, and subprogramme resource explanations for meeting and documentation services 2.206–2.216), so DGACM would be responsible for delivering services funded under that budget.
ai_comments.67: Requests the Secretary‑General to ensure progressive implementation of relevant accessibility standards for the treaty body system and to provide reasonable accommodation for experts with disabilities to ensure full participation. DGACM’s PPB explicitly includes disability inclusion and accessibility measures for conference services (see 2.13 and specific references to accessibility services in duty-station subprogrammes 2.74–2.75, 2.101 and 2.141), and DGACM would be expected to implement accessible meeting arrangements and accommodations.
ai_comments.68: Decides to allocate a maximum of three official working languages for the work of the treaty bodies (with exceptional inclusion of a fourth) while preserving States’ rights to interact in any of the six official languages. This is a decision that directly affects language/interpretation coverage and costs. DGACM is the system-wide lead on multilingualism and is responsible for conference interpretation and multilingual documentation across duty stations (see 2.1(c), 2.3, subprogramme 4 interpretation/meetings services 2.59–2.66, and references to multilingualism coordination 2.9–2.11), and would operationalize and manage interpretation services consistent with this language allocation.

ai_comments.37: Requests the Secretary‑General to ensure, as far as possible, that all requests for conference services for meetings of regional and other major groupings are met, and requests the Secretariat to inform requesters early about availability of conference services (including interpretation). This directs the Secretariat to perform conference‑servicing tasks that DGACM’s programme budget shows it implements (planning, scheduling, interpretation and client liaison).
ai_comments.41: Requests the Secretary‑General to continue to provide adequate information technology support for conference services, within the existing resources of the Department, to ensure seamless operation during the capital master plan. Directly concerns IT support for conference services — a core DGACM responsibility (e.g., e‑deleGATE, gDoc, gMeets) described in the PPB.
ai_comments.43: Requests the Secretary‑General to continue to provide adequate support, within existing Department resources, to ensure maintenance of the Department’s IT facilities, implementation of the global IT initiative and delivery of high‑quality conference services. This is a direction to the Secretariat regarding functions DGACM performs (systems operation, maintenance and service continuity).
ai_comments.45: Welcomes measures to ensure access to and use of conference services for persons with disabilities (Accessibility Centre) and encourages the Secretary‑General to continue efforts and report. DGACM implements accessibility services (sign language, captioning, seating arrangements) as reflected in its PPB, so this mandates continuation/expansion of those Department functions.
ai_comments.46: Requests the Secretary‑General to continue to address accessibility of conference facilities as a priority and to report. This directs Secretariat action in an area DGACM implements (meeting accessibility services described in the PPB).
ai_comments.47: Requests the Secretary‑General to report on efforts to establish common performance indicators and single IT systems (gData, gDoc, gMeets, gText). These are DGACM‑managed integrated systems per the PPB; the paragraph directs action and reporting on systems DGACM implements.
ai_comments.48: Requests the Secretary‑General to complete internal reviews concerning accountability mechanisms and the delineation of responsibility between the Under‑Secretary‑General for General Assembly and Conference Management and the Directors‑General at Geneva, Nairobi and Vienna, and to report. This mandates the Secretariat to clarify management arrangements directly affecting DGACM’s governance and operations.
ai_comments.50: Requests the Secretary‑General to continue to seek ways to promote workload‑sharing among the four main duty stations and to report. Workload‑sharing of documentation and interpretation is a central DGACM function (reflected in the PPB), so this directs action in an area DGACM implements.
ai_comments.52: Requests the Secretary‑General to develop recruitment, subcontracting and outreach policies to take account of imbalances in the pool of language professionals and to report. DGACM’s PPB shows it leads recruitment, subcontracting and outreach for language services; this instructs the Secretariat to adopt policies that DGACM will implement.
ai_comments.53: Requests the Secretary‑General to ensure that all language services are given equal treatment and provided with equally favourable working conditions and resources. This directly concerns the language services DGACM is responsible for and mandates Secretariat action to secure equitable treatment and resources for those Department functions.
ai_comments.54: Requests the Secretary‑General to ensure compatibility of technologies used in all duty stations and that they are user‑friendly in all official languages. DGACM manages conference and documentation technologies (gDoc, gMeets, etc.); this directs the Secretariat to achieve technical harmonization that DGACM implements.
ai_comments.55: Requests the Secretary‑General to include information on the operation, maintenance and harmonization of conference management software (gData, gDoc, gMeets, gText) in the proposed programme budget. These systems are DGACM responsibilities in the PPB; the paragraph requires Secretariat reporting and resourcing for systems DGACM operates.
ai_comments.56: Requests the Secretary‑General to report on updates (cost‑benefit, quality preservation/control) of the experimental statistical machine translation system (Tapta4UN). DGACM leads translation and technology initiatives per its PPB; this mandates reporting on a tool DGACM would be implementing or overseeing.
ai_comments.58: Requests the Secretary‑General to continue to ensure that measures taken by the Department to seek Member State evaluation of conference services provide equal opportunities in all six official languages and to report through the Committee on Conferences. This explicitly names the Department and directs action on client satisfaction processes DGACM conducts.
ai_comments.59: Requests the Secretary‑General to continue to explore best practices and techniques in client satisfaction evaluations and to report regularly. DGACM is responsible for conference‑service client evaluation in its PPB; this directs the Secretariat to pursue and report on evaluation methods that DGACM implements.
ai_comments.60: Requests the Secretary‑General to intensify exploration of innovative ways to systematically capture and analyse feedback from Member States and chairs/secretaries on conference service quality, and to report through the Committee on Conferences. DGACM conducts these evaluations; the paragraph mandates further action and reporting in that area.
ai_comments.61: Requests the Secretary‑General to continue to seek evaluation by Member States of conference services, including through language‑specific informational meetings (not to exceed two per year), ensuring equal opportunities in six languages and compliance with resolutions. This directs Secretariat action for evaluation modalities that DGACM is tasked to run.
ai_comments.62: Requests the Secretary‑General to keep the General Assembly and the Committee on Conferences apprised of progress in achieving integrated global management and to provide up‑to‑date information on new initiatives under the Committee’s purview. Integrated global management is a DGACM remit; the paragraph requires reporting on initiatives DGACM implements.
ai_comments.63: Requests the Secretary‑General to provide in his next report information about financial savings achieved through implementation of integrated global management projects. DGACM implements the integrated projects (per the PPB); this paragraph mandates reporting on results of DGACM activities.
ai_comments.69: Requests the Secretary‑General to appoint the Under‑Secretary‑General for General Assembly and Conference Management as the Coordinator for Multilingualism responsible for Secretariat‑wide implementation of multilingualism. This explicitly assigns the Coordinator role to the DGACM head — a direct mandate tied to the Department’s PPB responsibilities on multilingualism.
ai_comments.70: Requests the Secretary‑General to ensure the support necessary for the Working Group on the Universal Periodic Review reports to be issued in all official languages in a timely manner and to report to the General Assembly. DGACM provides translation and documentation services; this instructs the Secretariat to provide support DGACM would deliver.
ai_comments.71: Reiterates the request that the Secretary‑General ensure strict respect for rules concerning simultaneous distribution of documents in all six official languages (printed copies and posting on Official Document System/UN website). DGACM is responsible for simultaneous issuance and document posting per the PPB; this is a clear direction affecting Department operations.
ai_comments.75: Urges the Secretary‑General to ensure the timely presentation of official documents to the Fifth Committee and to find a lasting and sustainable solution to late issuance, so as to guarantee intergovernmental process quality. Timely issuance of documents is a core DGACM mandate in the PPB; this paragraph directs Secretariat measures DGACM implements or supports.
ai_comments.82: Requests the Secretary‑General to include in senior managers’ compacts a new standard managerial indicator related to timely issuance of official documentation to intergovernmental bodies and General Assembly committees, and to report in the next progress report on accountability. This instructs Secretariat management arrangements tied to document timeliness — an outcome DGACM’s work directly affects and reports on.
ai_comments.83: Requests the Secretary‑General to include in each section of the proposed programme budget an expected accomplishment of the Secretariat related to timely submission of documentation needed for meetings of relevant intergovernmental bodies. This mandates budgetary/result reporting on document submission — directly connected to DGACM responsibilities for documentation and scheduling.
ai_comments.88: Reiterates request that the Secretary‑General enforce the slotting system more rigorously (e.g., via the interdepartmental task force on documentation) and to report, noting only 84% of author departments reached compliance. This directs Secretariat enforcement measures to improve document submission predictability — matters DGACM monitors and acts upon in its PPB.
ai_comments.92: Welcomes interactions between the Department for General Assembly and Conference Management and author departments on waiver management, and requests the Secretary‑General to ensure continuous efforts in this regard and to report. This explicitly names DGACM and directs continuation of interdepartmental processes DGACM chairs/implements.
ai_comments.112: Requests the Secretary‑General to hold competitive examinations for recruitment of language staff sufficiently in advance to fill vacancies and to inform the General Assembly of efforts. Recruitment of language staff is a DGACM function described in the PPB; this mandates Secretariat action that DGACM will operationalize.
ai_comments.113: Requests the Secretary‑General to enhance access to competitive examinations by bringing examination sites closer to applicants in all regions and to report on progress. This directs Secretariat recruitment measures for language services that DGACM undertakes.
ai_comments.114: Requests the Secretary‑General to continue to improve the quality of translation of documents into the six official languages, giving particular significance to accuracy. DGACM’s PPB shows responsibility for translation quality management; this paragraph mandates Secretariat action to enhance translation quality DGACM implements.
ai_comments.116: Stresses the need to ensure the highest possible quality of contractual and in‑house translation and requests the Secretary‑General to report on measures to be taken. This directs Secretariat steps on translation quality control — a function DGACM oversees in its documentation services.
ai_comments.117: Reiterates request that the Secretary‑General provide, at all duty stations, adequate staff at appropriate levels to ensure quality control for external translation, with due consideration of equal grade for equal work. This mandates Secretariat resourcing that DGACM would implement to secure translation quality across duty stations.
ai_comments.118: Requests the Secretary‑General to apply common standards for quality control of documents processed by external translators in all four duty stations, within existing resources, and to report. DGACM’s PPB includes quality assurance for translation; this directs Secretariat‑level standardization that DGACM would operationalize.
ai_comments.119: Requests the Secretary‑General to report on experience, lessons learned and best practices of main duty stations in performing quality control of contractual and in‑house translations, including staffing requirements. This requests reporting on activities DGACM conducts and manages in its documentation services.
ai_comments.120: Encourages the Secretary‑General to establish globally standardized performance indicators and costing models for a cost‑effective strategy for in‑house processing of documents and requests submission of such information to the General Assembly. DGACM manages performance indicators and costing for documentation (PPB); this paragraph mandates Secretariat action in areas DGACM administers.
ai_comments.121: Notes measures taken by the Secretary‑General to address replacement of retiring staff in language services and requests continuation/intensification of efforts, including strengthening cooperation with training institutions. DGACM’s PPB includes outreach and training for language capacity; this directs Secretariat and Department activities to replenish language staff.
ai_comments.122: Requests the Secretary‑General to use appropriate means to improve the internship programme (to avoid shortages and turnover in language career fields) and to partner with organizations that promote official languages. DGACM conducts outreach/traineeships per its PPB; this paragraph mandates expansion of those Department activities.
ai_comments.124: Welcomes existing memorandums of understanding between the Organization and universities to strengthen training of language professionals and requests the Secretary‑General to continue efforts to assess the appropriate number of MOUs. DGACM’s PPB documents engagement with universities (MOUs); this paragraph directs continuation/expansion of that DGACM work.
ai_comments.125: Requests the Secretary‑General to make further concerted efforts to promote outreach programmes (traineeships, internships), introduce innovative methods to increase awareness, partner with Member States and institutions, and to report. DGACM leads outreach and internships in the language services; this mandates Secretariat action DGACM implements.
ai_comments.127: Requests the Secretary‑General to ensure that the Department for General Assembly and Conference Management, in cooperation with the Office of Human Resources Management, continues its efforts to raise awareness among Member States about employment and internship opportunities in the language services and to report to the Assembly. This explicitly directs the Department (DGACM) to continue specific outreach and recruitment activities named in its PPB.
ai_comments.128: Requests the Secretary‑General to develop the traineeship initiative further, extend it to all duty stations and to report. DGACM runs traineeship programmes per its PPB; this paragraph mandates expansion of those Department initiatives.
ai_comments.132: Requests the Secretary‑General, through the Department, to improve and expand the list of universities having memorandums of understanding with the United Nations, ensuring inclusion of institutions in all geographical regions whenever possible. This explicitly directs action 'through the Department' (DGACM) on MOUs and outreach — activities described in the PPB.

ai_comments.48: Operative para 17 requests the Secretary‑General to establish a special voluntary trust fund to assist developing countries in attending UN‑Habitat Assembly and Executive Board sessions. The Department for General Assembly and Conference Management (DGACM) has oversight and operational roles for conference‑related extrabudgetary resources (see PPB paragraphs on extrabudgetary trust funds and oversight). Thus this paragraph directs the Secretariat to create a fund whose oversight/administration and use for conference participation logistics would fall within activities DGACM implements (conference servicing, registration, trust‑fund oversight for conference management).
ai_comments.49: Operative para 18 requests the Secretary‑General to submit a progress report to the General Assembly at its seventy‑fifth session entitled “Follow‑up to the implementation of the New Urban Agenda and strengthening of UN‑Habitat”. DGACM’s PPB shows the Department is responsible for substantive and technical secretariat support and for preparation, processing and publication of Secretary‑General reports and parliamentary documentation for the General Assembly. Therefore this paragraph creates an implementation task for the Secretariat that DGACM will support (preparing, processing, issuing and making available the requested report).
ai_comments.50: Operative para 19 decides that the General Assembly should include, at its seventy‑fifth session, an item entitled “Follow‑up to the implementation of the New Urban Agenda and strengthening of UN‑Habitat” in its provisional agenda. Inclusion of a provisional agenda item is an action that the Secretariat (DGACM) implements in its role providing procedural secretariat services to the Assembly (preparing provisional agendas, agenda documentation and related secretariat follow‑up). Thus the paragraph imposes a concrete Secretariat task that DGACM’s PPB shows it carries out.

ai_comments.25: Requests the Secretariat to continue to provide notes for the Presidents of the main organs and Chairs of their subsidiary bodies in the United Nations official language spoken by the presiding officer — a Secretariat-level instruction that maps to DGACM’s mandate to provide procedural and technical secretariat support to the General Assembly and its committees (see PPB paras 2.1(a) and Subprogramme 1 activities). DGACM would be an implementing service for this task.
ai_comments.55: Requests the Secretary‑General to complete uploading important older United Nations documents to the UN website in all six official languages — directs the Secretariat to make multilingual parliamentary/archive documents available, which DGACM implements through its documentation and publishing services (PPB paras 2.1(c), Subprogramme 3 on documentation services and Subprogramme 4 on publishing).
ai_comments.56: Requests the Secretary‑General to continue to ensure, through provision of documentation services and meetings and publishing services under conference management (including high‑quality translation and interpretation), effective multilingual communication equally in all official languages — a clear directive to provide the exact services DGACM is mandated to deliver (PPB paras 2.1(a),(c),(d); Subprogrammes 3 and 4).
ai_comments.57: Encourages the Department for General Assembly and Conference Management, within existing resources and upon request, to document policy guidance regarding translation outsourcing and quality standards for use by relevant departments/offices — an explicit request directed at DGACM, matching its documentation, terminology and quality‑management responsibilities (PPB paras 2.46–2.47 on translation, quality assurance and leadership on gText/gDoc projects).
ai_comments.60: Reiterates request that the Secretary‑General ensure strict respect for rules on simultaneous distribution of documents in all six official languages (printed and online) — a Secretariat‑level obligation implemented operationally by DGACM’s documentation and publishing services responsible for simultaneous issuance (PPB Subprogramme 3 and 4, and PPB emphasis on simultaneous issuance e.g., paras 2.46–2.54).
ai_comments.61: Reiterates need to fully implement rule 55 (Journal of the United Nations shall be published in the languages of the Assembly) — directs Secretariat action to publish the Journal in all languages; DGACM operates the Journal/meeting‑information platforms in duty stations (PPB paras 2.101 on the Journal of the United Nations and Subprogramme 2/4 responsibilities for digital meeting information).
ai_comments.66: Encourages continuation of live webcasts and requests the Department of Global Communications, the Office of Information and Communications Technology and the Department for General Assembly and Conference Management to collaborate, on a cost‑neutral basis, to explore cost‑efficient technological options to ensure equal availability, searchability and user‑friendly presentation of webcast archives in all official languages — an explicit instruction naming DGACM to collaborate on a task squarely within DGACM’s remit to provide multilingual meeting/webcast and publishing services and to develop technological solutions (PPB paras 2.59, 2.67, 2.226–2.229 on digital/webcasting, eJournal, e‑services and the Global Innovation and Data Analytics Service).

ai_comments.2: Directs the Secretariat to continue updating regularly and equally the multilingual web page devoted to the revitalization of the work of the General Assembly in all six official languages. This is a clear instruction to the Secretariat to provide and maintain multilingual web content. DGACM’s programme budget (see Mandates and background and sections on multilingualism, coordination and digital platforms) identifies the Department as the Secretariat service responsible for multilingualism coordination and for conference- and Assembly-related web/e‑services (e.g., e‑deleGATE, iGov and related multilingual portals). Therefore paragraph 2 creates a Secretariat-level task that DGACM is expected to implement (maintain and update the multilingual web page).

ai_comments.42: Operative paragraph 15 requests the Secretary‑General to support the commemoration of UNEP@50 and invites voluntary contributions for its preparation and participation. Implementation of that request will require Secretariat support for the event (conference planning and management, multilingual meeting and documentation services where applicable, protocol and host‑country liaison, participant registration and facilitation). Those are squarely within DGACM’s remit as set out in its PPB (e.g., PPB paras. 2.1(c) on conference‑servicing support including at Nairobi, 2.1(d) on protocol and host country liaison services, and the Office of the Under‑Secretary‑General responsibilities in 2.201–2.202). Thus the paragraph creates a task for the Secretary‑General that DGACM is the entity within the Secretariat normally responsible for implementing.
ai_comments.45: Operative paragraph 18 decides to include, in the provisional agenda of the General Assembly’s seventy‑seventh session, the sub‑item 'Report of the United Nations Environment Assembly'. By placing the item on the Assembly agenda the General Assembly effectively requires Secretariat servicing of that agenda item (preparation and issuance of documentation, agenda management, meeting servicing and other secretariat functions). DGACM’s PPB explicitly assigns it responsibility for facilitation and substantive/technical secretariat support to the General Assembly and its agenda items (see PPB para. 2.1(a) and the subprogramme 1 description of providing technical secretariat services), so this decision entails implementation tasks for DGACM.

ai_comments.26: Operative paragraph requests the Secretariat to continue to provide procedural notes, statements and remarks for Presidents and Chairs in the United Nations official language spoken by the presiding officer. DGACM’s PPB (see overall orientation and subprogramme 1: para. 2.1(a), 2.1(d) and subprogramme responsibilities) shows that the Department provides procedural and technical secretariat support to the General Assembly, its committees and subsidiary organs. This paragraph therefore creates an obligation implemented in practice by DGACM through its procedural secretariat services.
ai_comments.72: Operative paragraph requests the Department of Global Communications, the Office of Information and Communications Technology and the Department for General Assembly and Conference Management to collaborate to explore cost‑efficient technological options to ensure equal availability, searchability, completeness and user‑friendly presentation of webcast archives in all official languages on the United Nations website, and requests the Secretary‑General to report on results. This explicitly directs DGACM to collaborate on a technical/multilingual archival task. It connects to DGACM’s PPB role in Secretariat‑wide coordination of multilingualism (para. 2.3), and to its responsibility for meetings, publishing and digital platforms (subprogramme 4 and programme support, paras. 2.59, 2.67, 2.226–2.229), which is the area in which DGACM would implement the requested collaboration.
ai_comments.85: Operative paragraph requests the Secretary‑General to continue to ensure, through the provision of documentation services and meetings and publishing services under conference management, including high‑quality translation and interpretation, effective multilingual communication equally in all the official languages among representatives of Member States in intergovernmental organs and United Nations expert bodies. While addressed to the Secretary‑General, this directs action ‘through … conference management’ — the functions that DGACM carries out (documentation services; meetings and publishing; translation and interpretation are core DGACM functions described throughout the PPB, e.g., paras. 2.1(a),(c) and subprogrammes 3 and 4). Thus it imposes an implementable obligation on DGACM’s service delivery.
ai_comments.86: Operative paragraph encourages the Department for General Assembly and Conference Management, upon request, to document policy guidance regarding translation outsourcing and quality standards for use by relevant departments and offices of the Secretariat. This is an explicit request to DGACM. It aligns directly with the Department’s documented remit to provide documentation services, translation quality management and terminology support (see subprogramme 3 strategy and planned results, paras. 2.46, 2.52–2.53), and thus constitutes a mandate‑giving paragraph for DGACM.

ai_comments.43: Requests the Secretary-General, in cooperation with the institutes of the United Nations crime prevention and criminal justice programme network, to prepare a discussion guide for the regional preparatory meetings for the Fifteenth Congress and for the Congress itself. This is an instruction to the Secretariat to produce conference documentation. The Department for General Assembly and Conference Management (DGACM) explicitly lists documentation, publishing and conference-servicing responsibilities in its PPB (see subprogramme 3: documentation services — e.g., para. 2.46 on delivering multilingual documentation, and subprogramme 4 on publishing services, para. 2.59). DGACM would therefore be expected to implement the preparation, publication and distribution aspects of the requested discussion guide (production, translation, simultaneous issuance and dissemination platforms).
ai_comments.44: Also requests the Secretary-General to facilitate the organization of the regional preparatory meetings and to make available the necessary resources for the participation of the least developed countries in those meetings and in the Fifteenth Congress. This is a Secretariat-level mandate to organize meetings and provide participant support. DGACM’s PPB explicitly assigns it the planning and management of meetings and provision of conference services, including liaison, registration and support for delegates (see paras. 2.1(a),(c),(d); subprogramme 2 on planning and coordination of conference services, para. 2.33). Thus DGACM would be expected to implement the operational/ logistical and conference-servicing elements of this request (meeting planning, registration/participant facilitation, publishing and distribution of documents, and host/participant liaison).
ai_comments.48: Requests the Secretary-General to facilitate the organization of ancillary meetings of non-governmental and professional organizations participating in the Fifteenth Congress, as well as meetings of professional and geographical interest groups, and to take appropriate measures to encourage participation of the academic and research community. The facilitation and organization of ancillary/side events and related registration/rooming/logistics are core conference-management functions. DGACM’s mandate and programme plan cover provision of conference-servicing and meeting support (see para. 2.1(c) and subprogramme 2 on planning and coordination of conference services, para. 2.33, and para. 2.202 on the Protocol and Liaison Service). DGACM would therefore be expected to implement the Secretariat’s facilitation of ancillary meetings and related participant engagement measures.
ai_comments.53: Requests the Secretary-General to ensure proper follow-up to the present resolution and to report thereon to the General Assembly through the Commission at its thirty-third session. This places an obligation on the Secretariat to coordinate follow-up and reporting. DGACM’s PPB identifies the Department’s role in facilitating orderly conduct of intergovernmental bodies and follow-up actions and providing substantive and technical secretariat support to commissions and committees (see para. 2.1(a) and subprogramme 1 on General Assembly and Economic and Social Council affairs, paras. 2.19–2.20). DGACM would be expected to support or implement the secretariat, documentation and reporting functions needed to satisfy this follow-up request (e.g., preparing and issuing the relevant documentation, servicing the Commission session where the report is considered).
ai_comments.54: Also requests the Secretary-General to submit to the General Assembly at its seventy-ninth session a report on the implementation of the present resolution. This is an instruction to the Secretariat to prepare and submit an implementation report. DGACM’s programme includes the preparation, publication and issuance of parliamentary documentation and reports (subprogramme 3 on documentation services and subprogramme 4 on meetings and publishing services, paras. 2.46 and 2.59). DGACM would therefore be expected to carry out the operational work of producing, translating, publishing and issuing the Secretary-General’s report as part of the Secretariat’s implementation of this paragraph.
