ai_comments.28: Requests the Secretary‑General to ensure adequate human oversight and appropriate quality control for multilingual online content generated through translation tools. DGACM (via the Office of the Under‑Secretary‑General and the Coordinator for Multilingualism hosted in the Department) is the Secretariat entity responsible for Secretariat‑wide multilingualism coordination and for overseeing quality of multilingual services (see PPB paras 2.3, 2.9 and subprogramme descriptions on documentation/technology). This SG request will be implemented operationally by DGACM units responsible for translation tools and multilingual quality control.
ai_comments.29: Requests the Secretariat to continue to provide procedural notes, statements and remarks for Presidents/Chairs in the United Nations official language spoken by the presiding officer. DGACM’s Subprogramme 1 provides procedural and technical secretariat support to the General Assembly and its committees (PPB paras 2.1(a), 2.20). This operative paragraph therefore imposes an operational obligation that DGACM implements through its procedural support services.
ai_comments.30: Requests the Secretary‑General to ensure that updates to the Procurement Manual are reflected in all six official language versions in an appropriate time frame. DGACM’s documentation and translation services (Subprogramme 3 and publishing services) are the Secretariat units that produce authoritative multilingual versions of official texts (PPB paras 2.1(c), 2.46–2.47). The SG direction will therefore be carried out in practice by DGACM translation/publishing teams.
ai_comments.35: Requests the Secretary‑General to implement the United Nations Strategic Framework on Multilingualism. DGACM houses the Coordinator for Multilingualism and is designated in the PPB as responsible for Secretariat‑wide coordination of multilingualism (PPB para 2.3) and for facilitating a coordinated approach (para 2.9). Implementation of the Framework will therefore be executed through DGACM functions.
ai_comments.36: Recognizes the need to strengthen the human resources capacity of the Office of the Coordinator for Multilingualism and requests the Secretary‑General to submit a proposal (including budget estimates). The paragraph directs resource/action on the Office that is located within DGACM (PPB para 2.3 references the Coordinator and Office of the Coordinator for Multilingualism). It therefore relates directly to DGACM’s staffing/capacity to carry out its mandated coordination role.
ai_comments.38: Requests the Secretary‑General to issue the relevant administrative and operational guidelines for implementation of the United Nations Strategic Framework on Multilingualism. Those operational guidelines will be implemented by the Coordinator for Multilingualism and Secretariat units; DGACM (hosting the Coordinator and responsible for Secretariat‑wide multilingual coordination per PPB para 2.3) will be a primary implementer of those guidelines.
ai_comments.39: Requests the Coordinator for Multilingualism and all Secretariat entities to contribute to implementation of the Framework. This is a direct instruction to the Coordinator for Multilingualism (the office located within DGACM) to take an active implementation role, matching DGACM’s stated responsibility to facilitate coordinated multilingualism across the Secretariat (PPB paras 2.3, 2.9).
ai_comments.91: Reiterates the request that the Secretary‑General complete the upload of important older United Nations documents to the UN website in all six official languages. DGACM’s documentation, meetings and publishing services (Subprogramme 3 and Subprogramme 4) are responsible for producing and issuing authoritative multilingual parliamentary/documentation products and for ensuring their availability online (PPB paras 2.1(c), 2.46–2.47, 2.59). The SG direction will therefore be operationalized by DGACM units.
ai_comments.92: Requests the Secretary‑General to continue to ensure, through provision of documentation services and meetings and publishing services under conference management (including high‑quality translation and interpretation), effective multilingual communication equally in all official languages among representatives of Member States and expert bodies. The paragraph explicitly references conference management services—DGACM’s core programme (PPB paras 2.1(a),(c); subprogrammes 3 and 4)—and thus constitutes a mandate that DGACM is the implementing service for.
ai_comments.95: Reiterates the request that the Secretary‑General ensure that rules concerning the simultaneous distribution of documents in all six official languages are strictly respected (printed copies and posting on the Official Document System/website). Ensuring simultaneous issuance is a central DGACM operational mandate (PPB paras 2.46–2.47, subprogramme 3 deliverables on simultaneous issuance), so this SG instruction will be carried out by DGACM documentation/publishing services.
ai_comments.112: Recognizes the contribution of the Language and Communications Training Unit and requests the Secretary‑General to ensure full implementation of the existing mandate on linguistic training. DGACM’s PPB describes learning, training and capacity‑building measures for documentation and language staff (see PPB paras 2.54–2.56 on learning and knowledge management, and subprogramme references to training in 2.46(b) and elsewhere). The SG request therefore relates to activities that DGACM and its language training functions deliver.

ai_comments.51: Requests the Secretary‑General, when implementing page limits for the Commission’s documentation, to take into account the Commission’s specific mandate and functions. This is a directive to the Secretary‑General on documentation policy that would be implemented by the Secretariat’s documentation and publishing services. DGACM’s PPB (subprogramme 3: Documentation services) explicitly states responsibility for delivering multilingual documentation services, applying quality/timeliness requirements and implementing documentation-related mandates, so this paragraph creates an obligation on the Secretary‑General that DGACM would operationalize (e.g., through how page limits are applied in document processing and issuance).
ai_comments.52: Directly requests the Secretary‑General to continue publication of Commission standards and to provide summary records of Commission meetings (including committees of the whole). Publication and provision of summary records fall within DGACM’s mandated functions (subprogramme 3: Documentation services; subprogramme 4: Meetings and publishing services), so this paragraph places a concrete task on the Secretary‑General that DGACM is responsible for implementing (i.e., continuing to publish Commission texts and to produce/provide summary records in the official languages).

ai_comments.65: Directs action: “Decides to include in the provisional agenda of its eighty-first session, under the item entitled ‘Sustainable development’, the sub-item entitled ‘Report of the United Nations Environment Assembly of the United Nations Environment Programme’.” This creates a concrete, procedural task to place that sub‑item on the General Assembly’s provisional agenda and to service it. Connection to DGACM PPB: DGACM is responsible for procedural and technical secretariat support to the General Assembly (see PPB para. 2.1(a)) including preparing agendas, servicing meetings and associated documentation. Implementation of paragraph 65 would therefore be carried out by the Department through its agenda‑setting, documentation and conference‑servicing functions.

ai_comments.68: Requests UN‑Habitat to finalize preparatory and organizational arrangements for the fiftieth‑anniversary commemoration and explicitly "requests the Secretary‑General to support the commemoration". DGACM’s PPB shows the Department is responsible for conference management, protocol, host‑country liaison and provision of Secretariat support for meetings and special events (see para. 2.1(a),(c),(d); executive direction and management paras. 2.201–2.203; and the various subprogrammes on planning and meetings). Operationally, DGACM would implement the Secretary‑General’s "support" by providing conference‑servicing, logistical and protocol arrangements and processing related documentation for the event.
ai_comments.69: Decides to hold a two‑day high‑level meeting of the General Assembly on the midterm review of the New Urban Agenda and "requests the President of the Assembly, in consultation with Member States and UN‑Habitat, to finalize the preparatory process and organizational arrangements for the meeting" and asks that the President submit an agreed declaration for adoption. DGACM’s PPB identifies the Department as the Secretariat unit that facilitates and provides the procedural, conference‑servicing and organizational arrangements for General Assembly meetings and high‑level events (see para. 2.1(a),(c); subprogramme 2 planning and coordination paras. 2.33, 2.207; and executive direction paras. 2.201–2.203). Thus this paragraph creates Secretariat/organizational tasks that DGACM implements (meeting planning, rooming, interpretation/translation/publishing and protocol support).
ai_comments.72: "Requests the Secretary‑General to submit a progress report to the General Assembly at its eighty‑first session on the implementation of the present resolution..." DGACM’s PPB includes responsibility for substantive servicing of the General Assembly, production and issuance of parliamentary documentation, and dissemination (see subprogramme 1 paras. 2.19–2.21 and subprogramme 3 documentation services paras. 2.45–2.53). DGACM would therefore implement parts of the Secretary‑General’s submission by processing, preparing multilingual versions, publishing and issuing the requested report and related documentation for the Assembly.
ai_comments.73: "Decides... to include in the provisional agenda of its eighty‑first session the item entitled 'Follow‑up to the implementation of the New Urban Agenda and strengthening of UN‑Habitat'." Inclusion of an item in the Assembly agenda triggers Secretariat actions (agenda preparation, scheduling, documentation and servicing). DGACM’s mandate covers facilitation and substantive/technical secretariat support to the General Assembly and its agenda items (see para. 2.1(a) and subprogramme 1 paras. 2.19–2.21), so DGACM would carry out the practical Secretariat work required to place the item on the provisional agenda and service the subsequent meetings.

ai_comments.619: Mandate: directs the Secretary‑General to convene the Conference of the States Parties not later than one year following entry into force. Connection to DGACM PPB: DGACM is responsible for providing substantive and technical secretariat support and conference‑servicing (planning, scheduling, meeting management) for United Nations conferences at Headquarters and duty stations. Convening the Conference will require the operational conference‑servicing functions (room scheduling, documentation, interpretation, registration, webcasting, etc.) that DGACM’s programme describes and normally implements on behalf of the Secretary‑General.
ai_comments.636: Mandate: requires the Secretary‑General to provide the necessary secretariat services to the Conference of the States Parties. Connection to DGACM PPB: DGACM’s programme explicitly states responsibility for substantive and technical secretariat support to United Nations conferences and intergovernmental bodies, including provision of meetings, documentation, interpretation and related secretariat services at Headquarters and other duty stations. This paragraph creates an obligation on the Secretary‑General to provide secretariat services that, in practice, DGACM implements.
ai_comments.637: Mandate: sets out specific secretariat functions — (a) assist the Conference and make arrangements and provide necessary services for sessions; (b) upon request, assist States Parties in providing information to the Conference; (c) ensure coordination with secretariats of relevant international and regional organizations. Connection to DGACM PPB: these enumerated secretariat tasks map directly to DGACM’s core functions (conference planning and coordination, documentation and information services, liaison/coordination with other secretariats and duty stations, and provision of meeting support and multilingual services) as described throughout the programme plan.
ai_comments.441: Mandate: requires the Secretary‑General to be notified of 24/7 points of contact, to keep an updated register of those points of contact and to circulate the updated list annually to States Parties. Connection to DGACM PPB: DGACM provides and maintains enterprise conference and information management services (portals, registers, documentation systems and dissemination platforms) and supports the management and circulation of intergovernmental information. Maintaining and publishing an updated register of contact points for the 24/7 network is an operational secretariat function that DGACM’s systems and services are positioned to implement on behalf of the Secretary‑General.

ai_comments.40: Explicitly affirms that the Department for General Assembly and Conference Management (DGACM) is responsible for implementation of policy, formulation of standards and guidelines, overseeing and coordinating United Nations conference services and overall management of resources — i.e., it confirms DGACM’s programmatic mandate described in the PPB (conference services, standards, integrated global management).
ai_comments.41: Requests the Secretary‑General to continue to explore technological and other innovations to advance effectiveness and efficiency in conference services and to report — a task DGACM implements in the PPB via its Global Innovation and Data Analytics Service and by leading enterprise IT projects (e.g., gMeets, gDoc, gText, eAPG).
ai_comments.44: Requests the Secretary‑General to ensure that new modules (e‑deleGATE, iGov, gData, gDoc, gMeets, gText) are implemented as enterprise systems and to report on operations/maintenance/harmonization — DGACM is the entity that develops, maintains and deploys these systems per the PPB, so this directs work that DGACM implements.
ai_comments.48: Requests the Secretary‑General to ensure that measures taken by DGACM to seek evaluation by Member States of conference service quality provide equal opportunities in the six official languages and to report — DGACM runs the global survey and client‑satisfaction processes described in the PPB, so this directs SG action that DGACM implements operationally.
ai_comments.49: Requests the Secretary‑General to continue to explore best practices and techniques in client satisfaction evaluations, to seek higher response rates and to report — DGACM leads client satisfaction evaluation (global survey) in the PPB and would implement these initiatives.
ai_comments.50: Requests the Secretary‑General to intensify exploration of innovative ways to systematically capture and analyse feedback from Member States and Chairs/Secretaries of committees and to report — DGACM is responsible in the PPB for client feedback mechanisms (global survey, analytics) and would carry out such systematic capture/analysis.
ai_comments.51: Requests the Secretary‑General to continue to seek evaluation of conference services at least once a year, guaranteeing Member States may present evaluations in any of the six official languages — DGACM operates these evaluation forums and the multilingual arrangements as detailed in the PPB, so this directs activity DGACM implements.
ai_comments.53: Requests the Secretary‑General to keep the General Assembly and the Committee on Conferences apprised of progress made in ensuring integrated global management and to provide up‑to‑date information on new initiatives — integrated global management and related reporting are functions DGACM carries out (PPB describes DGACM’s role in integrated global management and reporting).
ai_comments.59: Requests the Secretary‑General to ensure consistent and effective implementation of the terms of reference for the Coordinator for Multilingualism and to report — the Coordinator resides within DGACM per the PPB and DGACM implements Secretariat‑wide multilingualism coordination, so this directs work DGACM leads.
ai_comments.64: Requests the Secretary‑General to continue to take actions for effective implementation of timely issuance of documents for the Fifth Committee, taking into account stakeholders’ responsibilities, and to report — DGACM’s documentation subprogrammes are responsible for timely simultaneous issuance per the PPB and would implement these actions.
ai_comments.72: Requests the Secretary‑General to continue to take action on providing timely and simultaneous issuance of documents in all six official languages — this is a direct operational requirement that maps to DGACM’s documentation and publication responsibilities as described in the PPB.
ai_comments.73: Requests the Secretary‑General to continue to seek ways to promote workload‑sharing among the four main duty stations and to report — workload‑sharing of translation/editing/précis‑writing is explicitly managed by DGACM in the PPB (global management of documentation), so this directs DGACM implementation via SG coordination.
ai_comments.80: Requests the Secretary‑General to enforce the slotting system more rigorously through a dedicated focus such as the interdepartmental task force on documentation (noting the task force is chaired by DGACM), to report and urges author departments to adhere to deadlines — DGACM chairs the task force and is assigned the operational role in the PPB to facilitate submission and manage slotting, so this directs implementation by DGACM.
ai_comments.84: Requests the Secretary‑General to continue efforts to upload important older UN documents onto the UN website in all six official languages on a priority basis — digitization, publishing and online distribution are DGACM functions (subprogramme 4 and documentation services) in the PPB, so this directs activity DGACM carries out.
ai_comments.85: Requests the Secretary‑General to take all measures necessary to ensure that the digitization of key documents in the Dag Hammarskjöld Library and main duty stations is completed in a timely manner — DGACM’s publishing and document management responsibilities in the PPB map to implementing digitization and distribution, so this directs DGACM‑implemented work.
ai_comments.99: Requests the Secretary‑General to continue to maintain and update the global terminology portal (UNTERM) to ensure its availability to staff, Member States and the public — maintenance of UNTERM is a DGACM deliverable in the PPB (Subprogramme 3), so this directs activity DGACM performs.
ai_comments.100: Requests the Secretary‑General, as Chair of the UN System Chief Executives Board for Coordination, to continue to invite heads of participating funds, programmes and agencies to consider using official UN terminology and to report — DGACM/Coordinator for Multilingualism is the Secretariat‑wide lead for terminology (PPB) and would implement this outreach in collaboration with SG offices, so this mandates work DGACM undertakes.
ai_comments.101: Requests the Secretary‑General to continue efforts to develop recruitment, subcontracting and outreach policies relating to the pool of language professionals and to report — DGACM’s PPB includes recruitment, outreach to universities and subcontracting strategies (competitive exams, outsourcing), so this directs DGACM‑implemented actions.
ai_comments.102: Requests the Secretary‑General to ensure that all language services are given equal treatment and provided with equally favourable working conditions and resources — DGACM is responsible for Secretariat‑wide multilingualism coordination and for standards across duty stations in the PPB, so this is a mandate DGACM implements under SG direction.
ai_comments.104: Requests the Secretary‑General to take measures to ensure equal treatment of all six official languages, to address workload inequities arising from staffing structures and language specificities, and to report — DGACM’s PPB explicitly covers workload‑equity, staffing and technology adaptation across languages, so this directs DGACM implementation.
ai_comments.105: Reiterates the need for the Secretary‑General to ensure compatibility of technologies used in all duty stations and that they are user‑friendly in all official languages — DGACM’s Global Innovation and Data Analytics Service is tasked in the PPB to develop/maintain enterprise systems and ensure multilingual user‑friendliness, so this directs DGACM work.
ai_comments.106: Welcomes development of the computer‑assisted and machine translation system (eLUNa) and requests the Secretary‑General to report on updates (including cost‑benefit and quality control) — eLUNa is a DGACM tool referenced in the PPB (documentation/translation innovation), so this instructs activity DGACM implements and reports on.
ai_comments.110: Requests the Secretary‑General to intensify efforts aimed at filling vacancies in the language services (translation and interpretation) in a timely manner and to report — DGACM is responsible for recruitment planning and competitive examinations in the PPB and would implement efforts to fill vacancies.
ai_comments.111: Requests the Secretary‑General to continue efforts to address recruitment and retention of staff in language services and to ensure strategic workforce planning — this maps directly to DGACM’s workforce planning, training and recruitment activities described in the PPB.
ai_comments.112: Requests the Secretary‑General to continue efforts to hold competitive examinations for recruitment of language staff sufficiently in advance to fill vacancies and to inform the Assembly of efforts — DGACM conducts competitive recruitment examinations per the PPB, so this mandates DGACM action.
ai_comments.113: Requests the Secretary‑General to enhance access to competitive examinations (e.g., remote exams, closer sites) and to report — DGACM’s PPB includes improving recruitment methods and remote competitive examinations, so this directs DGACM implementation.
ai_comments.114: Stresses need to ensure highest quality of contractual and in‑house translation and interpretation and requests the Secretary‑General to report on measures taken — DGACM’s documentation quality‑control frameworks and interpreter management are core PPB functions, so this directs DGACM activities.
ai_comments.115: Reiterates request that the Secretary‑General provide, at all duty stations, adequate staff at the appropriate level to ensure quality control for external translation and freelance interpretation — DGACM is responsible for staffing and quality control arrangements across duty stations in the PPB, so this is an implementation mandate for DGACM.
ai_comments.116: Requests the Secretary‑General to apply common standards for quality control of documents processed by external translators at all four duty stations and to report — DGACM’s PPB describes strengthening performance management and quality assurance mechanisms for documentation and external processing, so this directs tasks DGACM will implement.
ai_comments.117: Requests the Secretary‑General to ensure experience, lessons learned and best practices in quality control are shared among duty stations and regional commissions — DGACM coordinates workload‑sharing, standards and best practice exchange in the PPB, so this mandates DGACM action.
ai_comments.118: Requests the Secretary‑General to ensure effective application of globally standardized performance indicators and costing models at the four main duty stations — DGACM is responsible for implementing standardized performance indicators and costing models as reflected in the PPB (reporting and harmonization), so this directs DGACM implementation.
ai_comments.119: Encourages the Secretary‑General to apply similar quality‑control measures for interpretation services, in particular freelance interpreters — DGACM manages interpretation quality and freelance interpreter arrangements in the PPB, so this directs DGACM‑implemented activity.
ai_comments.121: Requests the Secretary‑General to continue to improve the internship programme, including through partnerships that promote the official languages — DGACM’s PPB includes traineeships, internships and outreach to universities as recruitment and capacity‑building measures, so this directs DGACM implementation.
ai_comments.122: Welcomes memorandums of understanding between the Organization and universities to strengthen language training and requests the Secretary‑General to continue assessing appropriate number of MOUs — DGACM leads outreach and university partnerships in the PPB and would implement expansion/assessment of MOUs.
ai_comments.123: Requests the Secretary‑General to make further efforts to promote outreach programmes (traineeships, internships), introduce innovative methods to increase awareness (including partnerships with Member States and language institutions) and to report — DGACM’s PPB includes outreach and traineeship initiatives to replenish language capacity, so this is a mandate DGACM implements.
ai_comments.128: Requests the Secretary‑General to continue to improve and strengthen initiatives related to training and replenishing the Organization’s language capacity (including outreach programmes) — DGACM is responsible for training, learning and replenishing language capacity in its PPB and will implement these initiatives.
ai_comments.130: Requests the Secretary‑General to continue to liaise with permanent missions to identify outreach opportunities with universities and language centres worldwide to ensure availability of high‑quality language services — DGACM conducts liaison and outreach to universities and Missions per the PPB, so this directs activity DGACM carries out.

ai_comments.36: This operative paragraph explicitly addresses the interpretation and translation services provided by the Department for General Assembly and Conference Management: it recognizes operational challenges and 'encourages the Secretary-General to strengthen efforts to address these challenges, and engage with Member States and receive feedback on opportunities to enhance the quality and effectiveness of these services, for presentation to the General Assembly at its eightieth session.' Although the directive is to the Secretary-General, the PPB shows that DGACM is the entity responsible for delivering interpretation and translation (see mandates and subprogrammes on documentation, meetings and publishing services). Thus this paragraph creates an obligation for the Secretariat to take corrective action regarding services that DGACM implements and to present results to the Assembly, implying DGACM will be the implementing service and provide the technical input and follow-up called for.

ai_comments.161: Directs the Secretary‑General to ensure the United Nations Office at Nairobi remains a duty station, to continue efforts to attract more intergovernmental meetings to its facilities and to give intergovernmental meetings priority in use of the facilities. DGACM (conference management, Nairobi) is the Office’s operational arm for conference servicing and is responsible in the PPB for planning, managing and promoting meetings and maximizing utilization of Nairobi conference facilities; this paragraph creates an obligation that DGACM will implement operationally (scheduling, client outreach, prioritization of intergovernmental meetings).
ai_comments.162: Requests that utilization and management of the Nairobi conference facilities be in line with applicable criteria and encourages use of best practices and lessons learned from other UN conference facilities. DGACM’s PPB describes its role in optimizing capacity, harmonizing procedures across duty stations and applying best practices for conference management; this paragraph directs actions that DGACM is responsible for implementing in Nairobi (facility management practices, operational alignment with other duty stations).
ai_comments.163: Requests the Secretary‑General to provide updated information along with projected utilization rates for future meetings in the next progress reports. DGACM’s PPB includes responsibility for centralized planning, reporting and provision of performance/ utilization indicators for the duty stations; this paragraph mandates reporting and projection tasks that DGACM will produce and supply to the Secretary‑General for inclusion in the progress report.
ai_comments.164: Requests the Secretary‑General to ensure conformity with relevant building codes and standards, technology and workplace safety, and best practices for persons with disabilities in the design, construction and renovation of Nairobi facilities. DGACM’s PPB explicitly commits to ensuring accessibility of conference services and adjusting systems and seating arrangements for persons with disabilities; DGACM would be responsible for implementing or advising on accessibility and meeting‑space arrangements and ensuring meeting services conform to the accessibility and safety requirements referenced here.
ai_comments.154: Requests the Secretary‑General to ensure implementation of the Nairobi conference‑facilities project and the finalization of other ongoing major capital projects in a timely manner. DGACM’s PPB assigns the Department responsibility for managing and delivering conference services at Nairobi (including planning and coordination of conference services and engagement with host country); this paragraph creates an instruction to the Secretariat to implement the project—work that DGACM will operationalize on the conference‑services side.
ai_comments.156: Requests the Secretary‑General to ensure all project activities promote cost‑efficiency and transparency, are implemented within existing resources and in accordance with the UN legislative framework, and to provide detailed information in the next progress report. DGACM’s PPB emphasizes cost‑efficient delivery of conference services, resource planning, and adherence to rules; DGACM would be responsible for applying cost‑efficiency measures and supplying the operational detail required for the Secretary‑General’s reporting.
ai_comments.159: Requests the Secretary‑General to continue to proactively monitor and mitigate all project risks, to take all measures necessary to ensure delivery within scope, budget and timeline and to include an update on risk management and mitigation measures in the next progress report. DGACM’s PPB identifies responsibility for centrally coordinated evaluation, risk management and business continuity for conference services; DGACM would provide the operational risk information and implement mitigation measures for conference‑services aspects of the project.
ai_comments.160: Requests the Secretary‑General to ensure oversight, transparency and strict adherence to the legislative framework in procurement of goods and services for the project and to provide more detailed information in future progress reports. DGACM’s PPB describes procurement‑ and contracting‑related aspects of delivering conference services (e.g., contractual services for temporary staff, technology procurement); DGACM would be involved in procurement for conference‑services components and in providing the procurement detail requested for reporting.
ai_comments.167: Approves the establishment of three additional temporary positions for project management under section 29D (Administration, Nairobi) and three temporary positions under section 34 (Safety and security). These are concrete resource decisions for the Nairobi project that DGACM (conference management, Nairobi) will use to carry out project and facility‑management tasks identified in the PPB (planning and coordination of conference services, project implementation support).
ai_comments.168: Appropriates an additional amount of $23,132,000 for the Nairobi project in 2025 (detailed by budget sections). This appropriation provides funding for implementation of the Nairobi conference‑facilities project; DGACM is the Department responsible in the PPB for delivering conference services at Nairobi and will implement operational activities funded by this appropriation.

ai_comments.20: Creates an operational pathway for the Committee to transmit its documents and evaluations to the Secretary‑General “for publication and dissemination to States Members…” — this implicates the Secretariat’s publishing and document‑dissemination functions. DGACM’s PPB explicitly describes its role in publishing, distribution and multilingual documentation services (subprogrammes 3 and 4) and in making documents available to Member States and the public, so it would be the implementing service for the publication/dissemination called for here.
ai_comments.21: Directly requests the Secretary‑General “to provide the Committee with appropriate assistance in organising and carrying on its work, and to provide a secretary of the Committee.” That is an instruction to the Secretariat to provide secretariat support and a committee secretary — core functions that DGACM states in its PPB (provision of procedural and technical secretariat support, servicing of committees and conferences, and provision of secretariat services).
ai_comments.24: Requests the Secretary‑General to invite the Government of Japan to nominate a scientist to the Committee. This is an instruction to the Secretary‑General to undertake outreach/communications and nomination follow‑up; DGACM’s PPB identifies the Protocol and Liaison Service and executive/administrative components (executive direction and management, Protocol and Liaison Service) as providing protocol and liaison support to the Secretary‑General and servicing administrative matters, so DGACM would be involved in implementing such an invitation.
ai_comments.25: Decides to transmit to the Committee the records of the proceedings of the General Assembly on the present item. The Secretariat is responsible for preparing and transmitting Assembly records and parliamentary documentation; DGACM’s PPB describes responsibility for parliamentary documentation and servicing of the General Assembly and its subsidiary bodies, so DGACM would implement the transmission and provision of those records.

title: Rules Of Procedure Of The Conference On Disarmament
note: Includes membership of the Conference on Disarmament as of 1 July 2022 (p. 6).
corporate_subject: UN. CONFERENCE ON DISARMAMENT

ai_comments.20: Para 13 directs the Secretary‑General to appoint a Secretary‑General of the Conference to assist the Conference and its President in organizing business and timetables. This is a clear Secretariat task; DGACM’s PPB states it provides procedural and technical secretariat support and organizes meeting timetables and services, so DGACM would implement this requirement.
ai_comments.21: Para 14 requires the Secretary‑General to assist in preparing the provisional agenda and the first draft of the Conference reports to the General Assembly. DGACM’s subprogramme work includes substantive/procedural secretariat support and preparation/distribution of parliamentary documentation, so it implements this obligation.
ai_comments.22: Para 15 instructs the Secretary‑General, at the Conference’s request, to provide professional assistance by preparing background papers, bibliographies and compiling data relevant to negotiations. This maps directly to DGACM’s documentation and substantive secretariat functions (translation/compilation of materials, briefing papers).
ai_comments.23: Para 16 states the Secretary‑General shall perform such other functions as are entrusted to him by these rules or by the Conference. Although broad, this is an explicit delegation to the Secretariat; DGACM, as the Secretariat’s conference management arm, implements many such functions per its PPB (conference servicing, documentation, multilingual support).
ai_comments.24: Para 17 requests the Secretary‑General to provide the staff and necessary assistance and services needed by the Conference and any subsidiary bodies. This is an explicit requirement to furnish personnel and services (interpretation, documentation, meeting support) that DGACM’s PPB describes as core responsibilities.
ai_comments.31: Para 22 requires that, when requested, the Secretariat provide unofficial summaries of informal meetings in the working languages. DGACM’s PPB identifies provision of verbatim reporting, summaries and multilingual meeting services — this paragraph mandates that Secretariat service.
ai_comments.33: Para 24 provides that the Secretariat shall provide assistance to subsidiary bodies, as requested, including preparation of unofficial summaries. This directly tasks the Secretariat with services that DGACM’s documentation and meeting services subprogrammes deliver.
ai_comments.49: Para 37 mandates that simultaneous interpretation, verbatim records of public plenary meetings and documents be provided in UN languages. DGACM’s PPB explicitly covers interpretation, verbatim reporting and multilingual documentation services, so this paragraph establishes obligations DGACM implements.
ai_comments.52: Para 40 requires that verbatim records and formal and other relevant documents be distributed to States normally within two weeks and made available for public use. This imposes a clear documentation/distribution duty on the Secretariat; DGACM’s documentation and publishing subprogrammes are responsible for meeting such timeliness and publication mandates.
ai_comments.56: Para 42 directs that communications from non‑governmental organizations to the Conference, President or Secretariat be retained by the Secretariat, made available to delegations on request and that a list be circulated. This assigns a records‑management and distribution task to the Secretariat that aligns with DGACM’s document handling and publication responsibilities.
ai_comments.59: Para 44 requires that drafts of Conference reports be prepared by the President with the assistance of the Secretary‑General and be made available to all member States at least two weeks before adoption. This explicitly tasks the Secretariat with assistance in drafting and timely distribution—functions reflected in DGACM’s PPB.

title: Rules Of Procedure Of The Economic And Social Council
corporate_subject: UN. Economic and Social Council

ai_comments.201: Rule 6 directs that the President shall, through the Secretary-General, notify Members and other authorities of session opening dates. This creates an obligation on the Secretariat to issue official notifications — a task implemented by DGACM in its conference-management and meetings-planning functions (see PPB: conference management, planning/coordination of conference services; Protocol and Liaison Service activities).
ai_comments.213: Rule 9(1) requires the Secretary-General to draw up the provisional agenda for each session and submit it to the Council. Preparing and circulating provisional agendas and related documentation is a core secretariat function that DGACM performs (PPB: substantive and technical secretariat support to intergovernmental bodies; subprogramme 1 and conference-management activities).
ai_comments.236: Rule 10 instructs the Secretary-General to communicate the provisional agenda (after Council consideration) to Members, specialized agencies and others. DGACM implements agenda and meeting communications and dissemination (PPB: planning and coordination of conference services; use of e-deleGATE/eJournal to notify delegates).
ai_comments.241: Rule 11 requires that the provisional agenda for a special session be transmitted to the authorities listed in rule 10 at the same time as the notice convening the Council. This is an operational Secretariat task (issuing notices and agendas) that DGACM carries out under its conference-servicing and meeting-notification responsibilities.
ai_comments.245: Rule 12(2) states that supplementary items shall be placed by the Secretary-General on a supplementary list and communicated with supporting statements. That places a clear procedural duty on the Secretariat to compile and circulate supplementary agendas and documents — work done by DGACM (PPB: secretariat servicing, document management and communication platforms).
ai_comments.270: Rule 17 requires credentials and names of alternates/advisers to be submitted to the Secretary-General (and the Bureau to examine them). The registration/verification and handling of credentials and participant lists are tasks performed by DGACM's Protocol and Liaison Service and conference-management teams (PPB: paragraph 2.1(d) and Protocol and Liaison Service description).
ai_comments.323: Rule 28(1) provides that the Secretary-General shall act in that capacity at Council meetings and may designate a member of the Secretariat as his representative. This establishes the Secretariat's presence and representation role at meetings — functions operationalized by DGACM staff who provide procedural and technical secretariat support (PPB: subprogramme 1 and conference management).
ai_comments.324: Rule 28(2) requires the Secretary-General to provide and direct the staff required by the Council and be responsible for all arrangements necessary for its meetings. That directs the Secretariat to mobilize staffing and logistical arrangements — core DGACM responsibilities (PPB: planning/coordination of conference services; meetings and publishing services).
ai_comments.325: Rule 28(3) requires the Secretary-General to keep members of the Council informed of questions to be brought before it. DGACM implements member communications, scheduling and information distribution for intergovernmental bodies (PPB: e-deleGATE, iGov, eJournal and other delegate-facing platforms).
ai_comments.329: Rule 29(a) mandates that the Secretariat shall interpret speeches made at meetings. This is a direct operational mandate for interpretation services that DGACM provides (PPB: subprogramme 4 – Meetings and publishing services; interpretation services across duty stations).
ai_comments.330: Rule 29(b) requires the Secretariat to receive, translate and circulate documents. This directly maps to DGACM's documentation services (translation, editing, circulation) as described in subprogramme 3 of the PPB.
ai_comments.331: Rule 29(c) mandates that the Secretariat print, publish and circulate the records of the sessions, the resolutions of the Council and required documentation. DGACM's publishing and distribution activities (subprogramme 4 and publishing-related deliverables) implement this requirement.
ai_comments.332: Rule 29(d) gives the Secretariat custody of documents in the archives. DGACM is responsible for document management, archival custody and publication systems (PPB: documentation services and publishing operations).
ai_comments.333: Rule 29(e) requires the Secretariat to 'generally perform all other work that may be required.' This is a broad directive to the Secretariat to carry out ancillary meeting and documentation tasks — functions that DGACM carries out in delivering conference and document services across duty stations (PPB overall orientation and subprogrammes).
ai_comments.349: Rule 32 designates Arabic, Chinese, English, French, Russian and Spanish as the official languages and English, French and Spanish as working languages of the Council. This establishes a multilingual requirement that DGACM operationalizes as the Secretariat-wide lead on multilingualism and through its language services (PPB: paragraph 2.1(c) and 2.3 on multilingualism coordination).
ai_comments.353: Rule 33(1) requires that speeches made in an official language shall be interpreted into the other official languages. This is an explicit mandate for interpretation services — central to DGACM's meetings and interpretation functions (subprogramme 4).
ai_comments.354: Rule 33(2) allows speeches in non-official languages provided the speaker supplies interpretation into an official language and permits Secretariat interpreters to base interpretation on that. This prescribes interpretation procedures that DGACM must support operationally (PPB: interpretation and meeting support responsibilities).
ai_comments.356: Rule 34 requires that records be drawn up in the working languages and that translations be furnished on request. This directs the Secretariat to produce multilingual records — a core DGACM documentation mandate (subprogramme 3: simultaneous issuance and translation services).
ai_comments.363: Rule 35 mandates that all resolutions and formal decisions of the Council shall be published in the official languages. DGACM's publishing and documentation services are tasked with ensuring simultaneous multilingual publication in line with this rule (PPB: simultaneous issuance mandates and publishing subprogramme).
ai_comments.371: Rule 37 requires sound recordings of meetings to be made and kept by the Secretariat. DGACM operationally provides verbatim reporting, audio recording, transcription and related meeting-record services (PPB: meetings and publishing services; verbatim reporting/transcription targets).
ai_comments.374: Rule 38(1–2) mandates that the Secretariat prepare and distribute summary records of public meetings in the working languages, allow corrections, and distribute final records. DGACM undertakes preparation, editing, translation and dissemination of summary and verbatim records (PPB: documentation services and subprogramme deliverables).
ai_comments.387: Rule 40 requires that the text of resolutions and other formal decisions be distributed as soon as possible to members and participants and that printed texts be distributed after the session. DGACM's publishing, printing and distribution functions implement these obligations (PPB: subprogramme 4 publishing services; simultaneous issuance responsibilities).

ai_comments.28: Directs the Secretary‑General to draw up the provisional agenda for each session of the Economic and Social Council and to submit it to the Council. The Department for General Assembly and Conference Management (DGACM) provides procedural and technical secretariat support to the Economic and Social Council (see PPB 2.1) and would be the operational service responsible for preparing/drafting and processing those provisional agendas on behalf of the Secretary‑General.
ai_comments.29: Specifies that the provisional agenda for the organizational session must be submitted at least three weeks in advance. This is a timing obligation placed on the Secretary‑General that DGACM, as the secretariat service for ECOSOC, would implement by preparing and ensuring timely submission of the agenda.
ai_comments.30: Specifies that the provisional agenda for the substantive session is to be submitted at the organizational session. This places a procedural obligation on the Secretary‑General that DGACM would operationalize when compiling and presenting the substantive session agenda as part of its secretariat functions for ECOSOC.
ai_comments.31: Provides that the agenda for the organizational session shall include consideration of the provisional agenda for the substantive session. Although framed as an agenda-content requirement for the Council, this is part of the same rule governing agenda preparation and thus translates into an action DGACM must ensure when drafting and organizing the organizational session agenda on behalf of the Secretary‑General.

ai_comments.59: Text: “The Secretary‑General of the United Nations shall appoint the staff of the Commission, which shall form part of the Secretariat of the United Nations.” Task created: directs the Secretary‑General to appoint and establish the Commission’s secretariat staff. Connection to DGACM PPB: DGACM provides substantive and technical secretariat support to intergovernmental and expert bodies and manages conference‑servicing and secretariat functions (see programme description and Executive Office / programme support sections). While the paragraph instructs the Secretary‑General, the operational implementation (staffing the Commission’s secretariat, onboarding, and providing day‑to‑day secretariat support and conference services) is carried out within the Secretariat by Departments such as DGACM (Executive Office and conference‑servicing units), so this paragraph creates an action the Department is expected to operationally support.
ai_comments.61: Text: “The first session of the Commission shall be called by the Secretary‑General of the United Nations as soon as practicable after the Commission has been created by the Economic and Social Council.” Task created: directs the Secretary‑General to convene the Commission’s first session. Connection to DGACM PPB: DGACM is responsible for planning, coordinating and providing substantive and technical secretariat and conference services for intergovernmental bodies and conferences (including calling/organizing sessions, meeting planning, documentation and conference logistics). Thus, although the paragraph addresses the Secretary‑General, DGACM would be the Secretariat entity implementing the practical arrangements (meeting convening, logistics, documentation and related conference services) required by this instruction.

ai_comments.23: Obligation: directs the Secretary-General to bring to the attention of all Council representatives communications from States or UN organs relevant to Council consideration. Connection to PPB: DGACM (through its secretariat and conference‑servicing functions) implements dissemination of such communications, agendas and meeting information (see PPB: mandate/background paras 2.1(a), and services for agendas/meeting information under subprogramme 1 and programme support).
ai_comments.25: Obligation: requires the Secretary-General to draw up the provisional agenda for each Security Council meeting (to be approved by the Council President). Connection to PPB: DGACM provides procedural secretariat support and prepares agendas and related documentation for intergovernmental bodies (PPB paras 2.1(a), subprogramme 1 activities and documentation/agenda preparation functions).
ai_comments.28: Obligation: requires the Secretary-General to communicate the provisional agenda to representatives at least three days before a meeting (or simultaneously in urgent cases). Connection to PPB: the Department is responsible for timely distribution/communication of agendas and meeting materials (documentation and conference‑management functions described across subprogrammes, notably PPB paras 2.1(a), 2.26–2.31 and subprogramme deliverables).
ai_comments.34: Obligation: directs the Secretary-General to communicate weekly to Council representatives a summary of matters before the Council and their stage. Connection to PPB: DGACM supports provision and dissemination of intergovernmental information and maintains portals and services (e‑deleGATE, iGov, Journal) used to inform Member States (PPB paras 2.20–2.23, 2.22 on iGov portal).
ai_comments.44: Obligation: requires the Secretary-General to examine credentials of representatives and submit a report to the Security Council for approval. Connection to PPB: DGACM’s Protocol and Liaison Service provides protocol support, registration and related administration for mission personnel and delegates (PPB paras 2.202 and Executive direction and management description).
ai_comments.64: Obligation: requires the Secretary-General to provide the staff required by the Security Council (part of the Secretariat). Connection to PPB: DGACM supplies procedural and technical secretariat staff for intergovernmental bodies and conference‑servicing (PPB paras 2.1(a),(c) and subprogrammes on meetings, documentation and staffing strategies).
ai_comments.66: Obligation: requires the Secretary-General to give notice of Security Council meetings to representatives. Connection to PPB: DGACM handles logistics, meeting scheduling and communications to delegations (PPB paras 2.1(a), 2.20 and subprogramme 2 planning/coordination of conference services).
ai_comments.68: Obligation: makes the Secretary-General responsible for preparation of documents required by the Security Council and for distributing them (normally) at least 48 hours in advance. Connection to PPB: DGACM’s documentation and publishing services (subprogramme 3 and 4) carry out preparation, translation, editing and timely simultaneous issuance of Security Council and other parliamentary documents (PPB paras 2.46–2.54, 2.67).
ai_comments.111: Obligation (normative rule): establishes the six official/working languages of the Council. Connection to PPB: DGACM is the Secretariat lead for multilingual conference‑servicing and Secretariat‑wide multilingualism, responsible for ensuring equal treatment of official languages across services (PPB paras 2.1(c), 2.2, 2.3 and multilingualism/coordinator responsibilities in paras 2.1 and 2.3).
ai_comments.113: Obligation: requires that speeches in any of the six languages be interpreted into the other five languages. Connection to PPB: DGACM provides interpretation services and manages interpreter resources and assignments (subprogramme 4 meetings and interpretation services, PPB paras 2.59–2.66 and duty‑station descriptions).
ai_comments.117: Obligation: sets out the arrangement when a representative speaks in a language outside the six Council languages, including that Secretariat interpreters may base interpretation on the first interpretation. Connection to PPB: DGACM supplies and manages Secretariat interpreters and related procedures (PPB paras 2.59–2.66 and protocol/interpretation responsibilities).
ai_comments.119: Obligation: requires verbatim records of Security Council meetings be drawn up in the languages of the Council. Connection to PPB: DGACM’s verbatim reporting and documentation services are responsible for producing verbatim records in the six official languages (subprogramme 4 and subprogramme 3 documentation functions; PPB paras 2.58–2.66, 2.61–2.64).
ai_comments.121: Obligation: requires that all resolutions and other documents be published in the languages of the Security Council. Connection to PPB: DGACM’s documentation and publishing services (subprogrammes 3 and 4) are responsible for translation, editing and simultaneous publication of resolutions and documents in the six official languages (PPB paras 2.46–2.54, 2.67, and publishing deliverables).
ai_comments.128: Obligation: requires that, subject to rule 51, the verbatim record of each meeting be made available to Council representatives and participating States not later than 10 a.m. of the first working day following the meeting. Connection to PPB: DGACM is responsible for rapid processing and issuance of verbatim records and managing resources to meet these timeliness requirements (PPB paras on verbatim processing and targets, e.g. 2.61–2.64).
ai_comments.143: Obligation: requires the Secretary-General to submit annually to the Security Council a list of records and documents that have been considered confidential, for the Council to decide their status. Connection to PPB: DGACM manages custody, classification and publication of Council records and implements Council decisions on confidentiality and access through its documentation and records processes (PPB paras on documentation/publishing and record management).

ai_comments.14: 2.5 requires that all delegations be made formally through an online portal and that delegatees inform themselves of the applicable regulations and limitations. This creates a clear obligation on heads of entity (including the Under‑Secretary‑General for General Assembly and Conference Management/DGACM) to accept, review and manage delegations via the portal — an administrative requirement directly linked to DGACM’s programme support and executive direction responsibilities for resource and authority management described in the PPB.
ai_comments.15: 2.6 provides that when an officer‑in‑charge or officer ad interim is assigned, authorities are automatically delegated to that person unless formally specified otherwise. This imposes an internal operational duty on DGACM to ensure continuity of delegated authorities during temporary appointments, which connects to the PPB’s emphasis on integrated global management, succession planning and continuity of operations.
ai_comments.16: 2.7 states that a delegation to a head of entity carries personal responsibility and that the Secretary‑General may enquire into or suspend delegated authorities. This places accountability obligations on the DGACM head and senior management (reflected in the PPB’s executive direction and management section) to exercise delegated authorities properly and maintain compliance.
ai_comments.18: 2.9 requires delegatees to promptly and fully comply with all reporting requirements set by the delegator and the Under‑Secretaries‑General. This obliges DGACM to meet reporting and oversight duties associated with any delegated financial or HR authorities, tying to the PPB’s descriptions of the Executive Office’s role in reporting, resource planning and implementation of accountability controls.
ai_comments.19: 2.10 obliges any staff member receiving delegated authority to exercise high standards of professionalism and to discharge accountability for implementing mandates. This imposes behavioural and procedural obligations on DGACM staff (interpreters, editors, managers) consistent with the PPB’s emphasis on quality, performance management and stewardship of resources.
ai_comments.27: 4.1 directs that heads of entity will receive notifications of delegations via the online portal and must acknowledge receipt. This imposes an action requirement on the DGACM head to use the portal to accept and record authorities, aligning with the PPB’s responsibilities for managing departmental authorities and administration.
ai_comments.28: 4.2 requires heads of entity to use the online portal to view delegation descriptions and to subdelegate authority (and to view subdelegations). This creates a procedural obligation for DGACM management to manage internal subdelegations through the portal — directly relevant to the PPB’s descriptions of the Department’s internal management, delegation of responsibilities and harmonization of operations across duty stations.
ai_comments.35: 5.1 obliges heads of entity to subdelegate selected authorities to staff, aligning authorities with responsibilities and ensuring segregation of duties, with subdelegations made through the portal. This mandates DGACM to formalize internal delegations (e.g., to programme support, duty station directors) in support of delivering the conference management and documentation services set out in the PPB.
ai_comments.36: 5.2 provides that, where the Department of Management Strategy, Policy and Compliance determines an entity’s mandate requires subdelegation of specific authorities to another head of entity, such subdelegation shall be made through the portal. This creates an obligation on DGACM to accept and implement inter-entity subdelegations (or request them) where mandates require shared execution, which connects to the PPB’s references to shared responsibilities among Headquarters and the Geneva/Vienna/Nairobi duty stations.
ai_comments.37: 5.3 requires that heads may suspend/amend/revoke subdelegated authorities through the portal, communicate reasons in writing to the delegatee, and maintain a record. This mandates DGACM management to maintain records of internal authority changes and communicate them formally — an administrative control tied to the PPB’s emphasis on governance, oversight and implementation of the delegation of authority framework.
ai_comments.38: 5.4 requires heads of entity to ensure that any changes to authorities are reflected in concomitant changes to subdelegations (via the portal). This imposes a duty on DGACM to keep its internal subdelegation structure aligned with any revisions to its delegated authorities, supporting the PPB’s functions around workforce planning, role alignment and standardized administrative processes.

ai_comments.8: Establishes the Department’s overall role to play a proactive and facilitating role in enhancing effectiveness and efficiency of intergovernmental activities — a broad mandate that underpins the entire PPB (overall orientation and programme of work across subprogrammes 1–4).
ai_comments.9: Mandates the Department to provide technical secretariat services and substantive support to the General Assembly and its main committees — directly implemented in the PPB under Subprogramme 1 (General Assembly and Economic and Social Council affairs).
ai_comments.10: Mandates the Department to provide technical secretariat services and substantive support to the Economic and Social Council and its bodies — reflected in PPB tasks and targets under Subprogramme 1 and the Department’s servicing of ECOSOC.
ai_comments.11: Mandates provision of secretariat support to the Trusteeship Council — corresponds to the Department’s servicing responsibilities described in the PPB (Subprogramme 1).
ai_comments.12: Mandates the Department to provide technical secretariat services to conferences and ad hoc/extraordinary meetings under UN auspices — implemented across PPB subprogrammes for conference management and meetings (notably subprogrammes 2 and 4 at duty stations).
ai_comments.13: Directs the Department to provide and coordinate meeting and documentation services for all intergovernmental organs and expert bodies at Headquarters and other locations (shared responsibility with Directors‑General at Geneva, Vienna, Nairobi) — directly reflected in the PPB’s integrated global conference‑servicing model and in subprogrammes 2–4 across duty stations.
ai_comments.14: Mandates the Department to provide technical and substantive secretariat services to the Committee on Conferences — implemented via the planning/coordination activities described in the PPB (subprogramme 2 and references to Committee on Conferences support).
ai_comments.15: Obliges the Department to provide advice to the Secretary‑General and Secretariat departments on matters relating to the bodies it services — aligns with PPB references to advisory/ procedural support functions (subprogramme 1 and executive direction).
ai_comments.16: Directs the Department to provide advice to presiding officers of UN bodies — reflected in the PPB’s description of procedural and substantive support (Subprogramme 1).
ai_comments.17: Mandates provision of protocol services to the Secretary‑General, Deputy Secretary‑General and visiting high‑level dignitaries, and host‑country liaison and, upon request, to the President of the General Assembly — implemented in the PPB under Executive direction and management and the Protocol and Liaison Service (sections on protocol services).
ai_comments.18: Mandates the Department to provide secretariat services to the International Annual Meeting on Language Arrangements, Documentation and Publications — mirrored in the PPB (paragraphs noting the Department chairs/serves as permanent Chair and provides substantive support).
ai_comments.19: Directs the Department to manage conference‑servicing resources at Headquarters and provide policy guidance on utilization of apportioned resources under Directors‑General at other duty stations — reflected in the PPB’s integrated global management approach and programme support (Global Innovation and Data Analytics Service, Executive Office).
ai_comments.20: Requires the Department to formulate budget proposals collaboratively with conference operations at Geneva, Vienna and Nairobi and present an integrated conference management budget to intergovernmental bodies — corresponds to PPB budgeting and programme support functions described throughout Part B (resource requirements and tables).
ai_comments.22: States that the Department is headed by the Under‑Secretary‑General and that senior officials perform functions set out in ST/SGB/2015/3 as well as the bulletin — establishes managerial responsibilities reflected in PPB governance and executive direction sections.
ai_comments.26: Assigns responsibility to the Under‑Secretary‑General for all Department activities and administration and for representing the Secretary‑General in related meetings — connects to PPB descriptions of executive direction and management (paragraphs 2.201–2.205 and related).
ai_comments.27: Gives the Under‑Secretary‑General responsibility to guide integrated global conference management, establish policies and standards and allocate conference‑servicing resources for optimal delivery — directly implemented in the PPB (sections on integrated global management, delegation of authority, and programme support/Global Innovation and Data Analytics Service).
ai_comments.28: Assigns the Under‑Secretary‑General the role of chairing the International Annual Meeting on Language Arrangements, Documentation and Publications — reflected in the PPB (noting the Department’s role as permanent Chair and coordination of multilingualism).
ai_comments.31: Identifies the Assistant Secretary‑General’s accountability to the Under‑Secretary‑General and that the post has specific functions — corresponds to PPB references to senior management roles in executive direction and integrated global conference management.
ai_comments.32: Mandates the Assistant Secretary‑General to assist the Under‑Secretary‑General (including assuming operational and policy‑setting responsibilities) — maps to PPB operational leadership duties and management of Headquarters activities.
ai_comments.33: Directs the Assistant Secretary‑General to act as Officer‑in‑Charge in the Under‑Secretary‑General’s absence — a managerial mandate implemented in departmental governance as described in the PPB.
ai_comments.34: Designates the Assistant Secretary‑General as focal point for integrated global conference management and additional reporting officer for heads of conference operations in Geneva, Vienna and Nairobi — reflected in PPB integrated governance and coordination across duty stations.
ai_comments.37: States that the Office of the Under‑Secretary‑General is headed by a Chief accountable to the Under‑Secretary‑General — defines internal management structure supporting PPB executive functions.
ai_comments.38: Mandates the Office to support the Under‑Secretary‑General and Assistant Secretary‑General in discharging their responsibilities — directly connects to executive support activities described in the PPB (Executive Office functions, coordination).
ai_comments.40: Directs the Office to provide overall coordination in preparation and revision of departmental inputs to the programme budget — implemented in the PPB (Part B budget tables and the Office’s budget coordination role).
ai_comments.41: Mandates the Office to provide support to the Under‑Secretary‑General in his role as Secretariat‑wide Coordinator for Multilingualism — reflected in the PPB (paragraphs on multilingualism coordination and Office of the Coordinator for Multilingualism).
ai_comments.42: Requires the Office to provide substantive and technical secretariat services to the International Annual Meeting on Language Arrangements, Documentation and Publications and the annual coordination meeting of conference managers — aligns with PPB references to those meetings and the Department’s coordination role.
ai_comments.43: Directs the Office to coordinate internal and external communication of the Department — corresponds to PPB references to coordination and stakeholder engagement.
ai_comments.47: Establishes the Director of the General Assembly and Economic and Social Council Affairs Division and accountability to the Under‑Secretary‑General — a management mandate reflected in PPB Subprogramme 1 leadership responsibilities.
ai_comments.49: Mandates the Division to provide technical secretariat services and substantive support to the General Assembly and its committees — directly implemented in the PPB under Subprogramme 1 (detailed objectives and planned results).
ai_comments.50: Mandates the Division to provide secretariat services and substantive support to the Economic and Social Council and most of its subsidiary and ad hoc bodies — reflected in Subprogramme 1 activities in the PPB.
ai_comments.51: Mandates the Division to provide secretariat services to the Trusteeship Council — corresponds to the PPB description of servicing responsibilities.
ai_comments.52: Mandates the Division to provide secretariat services to conferences and other ad hoc meetings under UN auspices — reflected in PPB cross‑duty‑station conference management activities.
ai_comments.53: Directs the Division to plan and organize activities and services related to sessions of the organs noted above — maps to PPB operational planning functions for subprogramme 1.
ai_comments.54: Mandates assistance to Presidents of the General Assembly and other presiding officers on conduct of work — reflected in PPB advisory and procedural support roles.
ai_comments.55: Requires the Division to advise delegations and Secretariat entities and to provide analytical briefs to senior officials on major deliberations — implemented in PPB (procedural advice, analytical information under Subprogramme 1).
ai_comments.58: States that the Protocol and Liaison Service is headed by a Chief accountable to the Under‑Secretary‑General — sets management for protocol functions implemented in the PPB.
ai_comments.60: Mandates the Service to provide protocol services to the Secretary‑General and Deputy Secretary‑General during meetings and visits of high‑level dignitaries — reflected in PPB sections on protocol and liaison services.
ai_comments.61: Mandates provision of protocol services to the President of the General Assembly — implemented in the PPB (Protocol and Liaison Service responsibilities).
ai_comments.62: Directs the Service to provide host country liaison services, registration of diplomatic personnel and processing of diplomatic privileges and immunities — corresponds to PPB Protocol Service deliverables.
ai_comments.63: Mandates accreditation services for delegates and participants (HQ and other locations the Department services), issuing badges/passes, ensuring compliance with protocol practice — directly implemented in PPB (paragraphs on accreditation and registration in Protocol and Liaison Service).
ai_comments.64: Requires the Service to provide briefings to newly arrived permanent representatives and organize presentation of credentials and periodic briefings on protocol practices — reflected in PPB Protocol Service functions.
ai_comments.65: Directs maintenance of up‑to‑date lists of Heads of State/Government and ministers, the diplomatic personnel database (Blue Book), and issuing official lists of delegations — implemented by Protocol and Liaison Service as described in the PPB.
ai_comments.66: Mandates organizing official ceremonies, luncheons, dinners, social events and photo opportunities hosted by the Secretary‑General or spouse at Headquarters — aligns with PPB Protocol Service event management tasks.
ai_comments.67: Directs assistance to permanent missions/observer missions with preparations for official visits of high‑level persons — implemented in PPB Protocol and Liaison Service activities.
ai_comments.70: Establishes the Central Planning and Coordination Division headed by a Director accountable to the Under‑Secretary‑General — sets leadership for functions implemented in the PPB (planning/coordinating).
ai_comments.72: Mandates the Division to develop and coordinate the biennial calendar of conferences and meetings worldwide and to schedule all meetings at Headquarters — directly corresponds to PPB planning and calendar functions (subprogramme 2 and Central Planning activities).
ai_comments.73: Directs coordination of the daily programme of meetings at Headquarters and at other locations for New York‑headquartered bodies — implemented in PPB (scheduling and meeting management tasks).
ai_comments.74: Mandates the Division to plan and monitor documentation processing schedules at Headquarters and coordinate with other duty stations to ensure workload sharing and compliance with timeliness and documentation control mandates — directly reflected in PPB (documentation and workload‑sharing measures across subprogramme 3 and planning).
ai_comments.75: Requires coordination of servicing meetings at locations away from established headquarters, as appropriate — implemented in PPB (conference management for meetings away from HQ).
ai_comments.76: Directs preparation of statistical and analytical reports on conference management activities at Headquarters and collaboration with other duty stations to ensure compatibility of statistical reports — corresponds to PPB reporting and performance indicators (see subprogramme 2 deliverables and performance measures).
ai_comments.77: Mandates providing technical and substantive secretariat services to the Committee on Conferences — reflected in PPB support to that Committee (references across subprogrammes).
ai_comments.78: Directs the Division to prepare and process the Journal of the United Nations — implemented in the PPB (references to Journal of the United Nations in Geneva and other duty stations).
ai_comments.81: Establishes the Documentation Division headed by a Director accountable to the Under‑Secretary‑General — management basis for documentation functions in the PPB.
ai_comments.83: Mandates translating all official UN documents, meeting records, publications and correspondence into and from the six official languages at Headquarters and other duty stations — core mandate implemented throughout PPB Subprogramme 3 (Documentation services).
ai_comments.84: Mandates translating selected materials into German — aligns with PPB references to the trust fund for German language translation and documentation activities.
ai_comments.85: Directs issuing summary records of meetings entitled to them in the working languages of the bodies concerned — implemented in PPB documentation deliverables and performance measures.
ai_comments.86: Requires editing drafts of parliamentary documents and preparing official records of meetings and sessions — corresponds to PPB functions of Subprogramme 3 (editing, desktop publishing, quality management).
ai_comments.87: Mandates issuing drafting and editorial guidelines for the Secretariat — reflected in PPB emphasis on quality assurance, translation quality management framework and terminology standards.
ai_comments.88: Directs maintaining the United Nations Terminology Database and providing on‑demand reference/terminology services to language professionals and reporters — directly implemented via UNTERM and referenced throughout the PPB (subprogramme 3 deliverables).
ai_comments.89: Mandates preparing and proofreading parliamentary documents and other materials for printing and electronic dissemination using text‑processing and desktop publishing — core activity in PPB Subprogramme 3 and subprogramme 4 publishing deliverables.
ai_comments.90: Directs processing and dispatching correspondence from the Secretary‑General, Presidents of main organs and Secretariat departments — an operational documentation mandate reflected in the PPB’s services and workflows.
ai_comments.93: Establishes the Meetings and Publishing Division headed by a Director accountable to the Under‑Secretary‑General — management basis for meetings and publishing functions in the PPB.
ai_comments.95: Mandates providing interpretation services in the six official languages for meetings at Headquarters and, per policy, at other locations the Department services — core mandate implemented across PPB Subprogramme 4 (Meetings and publishing services) and duty‑station descriptions.
ai_comments.96: Directs provision of meeting room services at all meetings at Headquarters and at other locations for New York‑headquartered bodies — implemented in PPB (meeting support, room logistics described in subprogramme 4).
ai_comments.97: Mandates preparing and processing verbatim records of meetings of the General Assembly, Security Council and other entitled bodies — reflected in PPB performance measures and planned results on verbatim records (subprogramme 4).
ai_comments.98: Requires developing and applying standards for typographic formatting of UN documents and providing guidance on electronic publishing best practices — implemented in PPB publishing strategy and investments in digital platforms and gDoc/gText projects.
ai_comments.99: Directs preparing and proofreading publications and other materials for printing and electronic dissemination using text‑processing and desktop publishing — aligns with PPB publishing and desktop publishing reforms (subprogramme 4 and coordination with subprogramme 3).
ai_comments.100: Mandates printing and distributing parliamentary documents, mandated publications and other materials in hard copy and/or electronic form through the Official Document System and other tools (including subscriber dissemination) — directly implemented in PPB deliverables (publishing operations, eSubscription, on‑demand printing).
